abstract: |
  We refine Mariño's large $N$ duality for the colored Kauffman invariant of $\mathrm{SO}(N)$ Chern--Simons theory within the orientifold refined topological string of Aganagic and Schaeffer. We define a refined crosscap invariant $g = f - \tfrac12 f^{\mathrm{cov}}$ from the $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ refined Chern--Simons invariants and those of the $\mathrm{U}(2N-1)$ cover. Assuming a classification of one-particle states modeled on that of Aganagic and Schaeffer, we derive from the M-theory index the structure $g = \tfrac12 E/(1+t) + C$, with $E$ a signed count of states invariant under the orientifold involution and $C$ a count of frozen states. From DAHA-Jones polynomials we obtain $g$ at general $N$ for two-strand torus knots with up to three boxes (four for the trefoil), for $T(3,4)$ in the fundamental representation and for two algebraic cables of the trefoil. In these cases the $N$-dependent poles cancel, $g$ is an integer Laurent polynomial up to the factor $2(1+t)$ predicted by the index in even sectors, and its refined part is divisible by $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)$. For the fundamental representation of $T(2,2m+1)$, $m \le 5$, the $c = 1$ part has a $G$-expansion whose coefficients have a common sign in each block up to the factor $(\boldsymbol{t}^2-1)$, and the $c = 2$ part is $-(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)$ times a positive polynomial; we conjecture this sign property for all $m$, which fails for $T(3,4)$ and the cables. The brane--brane sector of the cover reproduces the refined LMOV invariants of Kameyama and Nawata for the trefoil and $T(2,5)$ with up to two boxes, and we conjecture a closed form of the brane--image sector of two-strand torus knots as a space of states, checked for $T(2,3)$--$T(2,15)$. For higher representations the signs do not align; we conjecture that the obstruction lies in the multiplet structure of the frozen states.

# Introduction {#sec-intro}

## Background and questions

The $\mathrm{U}(N)$ Chern--Simons theory on $S^3$ is dual, at large $N$, to the closed topological string on the resolved conifold [@GV98], and its Wilson loops are dual to open topological strings ending on Lagrangian branes [@OV99]. In [@OV99] the generating function of the colored HOMFLY-PT invariants of a knot was reformulated as a free energy of such open strings, whose expansion is governed by integer BPS invariants; the integrality and the structure of this expansion were sharpened in [@LM00; @LMV00; @LM01] to what are now called the LMOV invariants (after Labastida, Mariño, Ooguri and Vafa), with the reformulation in terms of the matrix $M$ and the Adams operations that we use below. For $\mathrm{SO}(N)$ and $\mathrm{Sp}(N)$ the dual theory is the topological string on an orientifold of the Calabi--Yau [@SV00]. In the orientifold the BPS states are M2-branes wrapped on surfaces that may be non-orientable; the *crosscap number* $c \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ counts the crosscaps of the surface, $c = 0$ being the oriented states that also exist on the cover. It was conjectured in [@Marino09], and verified there in many examples, that the colored Kauffman invariant of $\mathrm{SO}(N)$ minus one half of the $\mathrm{U}(N)$ invariant in composite representations is expressed through integer BPS invariants with $c = 1, 2$ (see also [@BFM04; @BFM05; @PBR10; @Stevan10; @NRZ13]). Reformulated $\mathrm{SO}(N)$ link invariants with integer coefficients were obtained earlier in [@BR05], an orthogonal version of the LMOV conjecture was formulated mathematically and proved in special cases in [@CC10], and the integrality was tested for arborescent knots with up to two boxes in [@MMMRSS17]. The unoriented topological string and its BPS expansion were developed further as the real topological string [@Walcher07; @KW09], which has an M-theory interpretation [@PU14]. On the homological side, a Kauffman homology and superpolynomials for two-strand torus knots were proposed in [@GW05], and the relation between $\mathrm{SO}$/$\mathrm{Sp}$ invariants, composite representations and BPS states was studied in [@GS11].

Refined Chern--Simons theory was formulated in [@AgSh11]. For torus knots in the fundamental representation its invariants were found there to equal the Poincaré polynomial of the homology categorifying the HOMFLY-PT polynomial, the superpolynomial of [@DGR05], whose interpretation as a space of BPS states goes back to [@GSV04]; superpolynomials of torus knots have also been constructed from DAHA [@Cherednik11], by substituting Macdonald polynomials for characters [@DMMSS11], from Hilbert schemes [@ORS12; @GN13] and from the rational DAHA [@GORS12]. For the Hopf link, homological invariants were obtained from the refined topological vertex [@IKV07] in [@GIKV07] and related to the $S$-matrix of refined Chern--Simons theory in [@IK11] (see also [@MM20]). In [@KN17] a refined large $N$ duality was formulated for torus knots: the $\mathrm{U}(N)$ refined Chern--Simons invariants are reformulated into refined BPS invariants on the resolved conifold, which were conjectured there to be non-negative integers and found to be so in the examples computed. Positivity is expected because refinement resolves the BPS index by an additional spin: the cancellations of $(-1)^F$ in the unrefined index are undone and the coefficients become numbers of states. In [@AgSc12] the refined topological string on an orientifold was defined as an M-theory index, the $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ refined Chern--Simons invariants were computed, and the closed-string free energy at large $N$ was shown to satisfy the integrality of second quantization. The closed $\mathrm{SO}$ and $\mathrm{Sp}$ free energies were organized with multiple sine functions in [@AM22]. For open strings, i.e., for knots, to our knowledge neither a formula extracting refined crosscap BPS invariants nor a test of their integrality has been available.

The purpose of this paper is to supply both. We ask how a refined crosscap invariant is to be extracted from the $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ refined Chern--Simons invariants, and whether it has an integral BPS expansion and, if so, with what structure (a universal factor, the dependence on the winding number $d$, boundary factors). We then ask whether positivity becomes visible after refinement, in the sense that the coefficients align in sign in a suitable multiplet basis, and where this holds and where it fails. Finally, we ask how the invariant is related to the $\mathrm{U}(2N-1)$ cover, how much of the crosscap structure the cover determines, and what remains open for higher representations.

## Grading of statements {#sec-grading}

Statements are graded as follows. *Propositions* and *corollaries* are derived analytically, possibly under an explicitly stated hypothesis. A *Result* is a statement verified by computer, with the range of verification stated; negative outcomes of computations are reported as results as well, and are marked as such. *Conjectures* are closed forms or structures suggested by computation beyond the verified range. *Hypotheses* are rules that could not be taken directly from the literature; we say which verification supports them. Throughout, *(open)* marks a point left open. Computational methods and the verification ranges of the interpolations are collected in Appendix [A](#sec-app-code). Abbreviations: DAHA (double affine Hecke algebra), LMOV (Labastida--Mariño--Ooguri--Vafa), TN (Taub--NUT), CoHA (cohomological Hall algebra).

## Main results

The refined crosscap invariant is $g = f - \tfrac12 f^{\mathrm{cov}}$ (Definition [-@def-crosscap]), where $f$ is the free energy of the $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ refined invariants assembled with the dual Cauchy kernel of Koornwinder polynomials [@Mimachi01], and $f^{\mathrm{cov}}$ is the free energy of the A-type invariants of the cover in ordinary and composite representations (Hypothesis [-@exm-cover]). Both are taken in a uniform normalization fixed by determinant shifts and charge conjugation, and the BPS basis is reached with the reformulation matrix $M(q^{-1})$ of [@Marino09]. The normalization freedoms and how each is fixed are listed in Table [-@tbl-norm]. The definition is the subject of §[-@sec-setup].

The structure of $g$ follows from the M-theory index (§[-@sec-index]). Under a classification of one-particle states modeled on [@AgSc12] (Hypothesis [-@exm-classes]), the index gives $g = \tfrac12 E/(1+t) + C$ (Proposition [-@prp-alld]), with $E$ present only in sectors with equal numbers of brane and image boxes and with boundary factor $z_q^{n-1}(z_q^+)^n$ (Proposition [-@prp-boundary]); the separation of $E$ and $C$ is not determined by the index (Proposition [-@prp-EC]). Computing DAHA-Jones polynomials at generic $t$ and interpolating in $N$, we obtain $g$ at general $N$ for the trefoil with up to four boxes and for $T(2,5)$, $T(2,7)$, $T(2,9)$ with two and three boxes (§[-@sec-generalN]). Adopting the iterated DAHA-Jones polynomials of [@CD14] as the definition, we also obtain it for the $(2,13)$-cable of the trefoil (fundamental representation and two boxes) and the $(2,15)$-cable (fundamental representation), which we denote by $\mathcal{C}_{13}$ and $\mathcal{C}_{15}$ (§[-@sec-cable]). In every case the $N$-dependent poles cancel; $g$ is an integer Laurent polynomial in odd sectors and $2(1+t)g$ is one in even sectors, the $(1+t)$ sitting where Proposition [-@prp-alld] predicts; and the refined part is divisible by the universal factor $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)$ (Conjecture [-@cnj-structure]).

As for the signs, for the fundamental representation of $T(2,2m+1)$, $m \le 5$, the $c = 1$ part has a $G$-expansion whose $\lambda^\beta$ blocks have a common sign or are $(\boldsymbol{t}^2-1)$ times such a block, and the $c = 2$ part is $-(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)$ times a positive polynomial (Result [-@exr-torus]); we conjecture this sign property for all $m$ (Conjecture [-@cnj-criterion], §[-@sec-torus]). It fails for $T(3,4)$, where the $c = 1$ part is not $\sigma$-symmetric (§[-@sec-t34]), and for the cables (§[-@sec-cable]). For higher representations of the crosscap part the $c = 1$ part is not $\sigma$-symmetric and the signs do not align (§[-@sec-positivity]).

The cover is studied in §[-@sec-cover]. For the trefoil and $T(2,5)$ with up to two boxes, its brane--brane sector coincides with the refined LMOV invariants of [@KN17] and has aligned signs. Its brane--image sector is the source of $E$, and for two-strand torus knots we identify it, conjecturally, as a space of states whose only sign mixing is the subtraction of pairs in one block: the blocks are $\mathrm{Sym}^kV$, $\mathrm{Sym}^{2m}V - S\otimes S$ and corrections $F_{j'}$ (Conjecture [-@cnj-closedform], checked for $T(2,3)$--$T(2,15)$). The generating function of the blocks is expressed through the rows of the fundamental and adjoint representations by an identity (Proposition [-@prp-rows]); for fourteen torus knots we find that the block at which the universal series ends is $\mathrm{Sym}^{2\delta}V$ minus the square of the top two rows of the fundamental representation (Result [-@exr-rows]). From this identification, fitted on $T(2,3)$--$T(2,9)$, $E$ is predicted for $T(2,11)$--$T(2,15)$.

With the $C_N$ DAHA, the refined $\mathrm{Sp}(2N)$ invariants of [@AM22] satisfy $g^{\mathrm{Sp}}(\boldsymbol{a}) = -g^{\mathrm{SO}}(-\boldsymbol{a})$ in the fundamental representation of $T(2,3)$ and $T(2,5)$, and $W_R^{\mathrm{Sp}}(\boldsymbol{a}) = (-1)^{|R|}W_R^{\mathrm{SO}}(-\boldsymbol{a})$ for the trefoil with two boxes, refined versions of the classical $\mathrm{Sp}(N) = \mathrm{SO}(-N)$ correspondence (§[-@sec-sp]). What remains open is the structure of the multi-box invariants: the $\sigma$-asymmetry of the $c = 1$ part splits into a part present in the unrefined theory and a $\sigma$-odd part divisible by $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)(q_\ell- q_\ell^{-1})$. Since the cover is well behaved, we conjecture that the obstruction lies in the multiplet structure of the frozen states (§[-@sec-discussion]). The range covered by the computations is summarized in Table [-@tbl-summary].

The paper is organized as follows. In §[-@sec-setup] we fix variables and terminology, the kernel and the normalization, and define the refined crosscap invariant. In §[-@sec-index] we derive the all-$d$ structure, the boundary factors and the conditions that fix $E$ from the orientifold index. The unknot and the Hopf link are treated in §[-@sec-hopf], the fundamental representation of torus knots and the sign property in §[-@sec-torus], the integrality and the universal factor at general $N$ for higher representations in §[-@sec-generalN], the algebraic cables in §[-@sec-cable] and the refined $\mathrm{Sp}(2N)$ invariants in §[-@sec-sp]. In §[-@sec-cover] we split the cover into brane and image, §[-@sec-positivity] collects the obstructions for multi-box crosscap invariants, and §[-@sec-discussion] summarizes the status of the statements and the open problems. Appendix [A](#sec-app-code) describes the computations, Appendix [B](#sec-app-closed) the closed-string check, Appendix [C](#sec-app-fixed) further structure of the fixed sector of the cover, and Appendix [D](#sec-app-data) the generated tables of invariants.

# Refined crosscap invariants {#sec-setup}

## Variables and terminology {#sec-variables}

We use the following variables; the unrefined limit is $t = q$.

:::

At $t = q$ the variables of [@Marino09] are $t_M = q^{1/2}$ and $z = z_q$, and the $q_{\mathrm{NRZ}}$ of the Kauffman polynomial $F_R(K; \lambda, q_{\mathrm{NRZ}})$ of [@NRZ13] is also $q^{1/2}$. Young diagrams are written $R, \mu, \nu$ (never $\lambda$); in displayed formulas we draw them, e.g., $g_{\ydB}$, and in the text we write $(2)$, $(1,1)$ for the same diagrams; $(1)$ is the fundamental representation. Composite representations of $\mathrm{U}(N_A)$ are written $(\alpha;\bar\beta)$, the adjoint being $(1;\bar1)$. Some letters are reused with a local meaning that is stated where they occur (e.g., $r, s$ in $T(r,s)$, the $(Q, T, \mathsf X)$ of [@AM22] in Appendix [B](#sec-app-closed)).

We use the following terminology throughout. An invariant depending on $\lambda$ is split into its coefficients of $\lambda^\beta$, the $\lambda^\beta$ *blocks*; since $\boldsymbol{a}= \lambda$, we also call them $\boldsymbol{a}$ blocks. A block is *aligned* if all its coefficients (in the stated variables) have the same sign, and *mixed* otherwise. For the fundamental representation the *$c = 2$ part* is the part with odd powers of $\boldsymbol{a}$ and the *$c = 1$ part* the part with even powers (Definition [-@def-c12]); for hatted multi-box invariants the parity rule depends on the representation (Result [-@exr-multibox-sigma]). The *hatted invariants* are the BPS-basis invariants $\hat g = M(q^{-1})^{-1}g$ of Definition [-@def-crosscap], and the *refined part* of an invariant $\hat g$ is $X_1 = \hat g - \hat g|_{t=q}(\lambda \to \tilde\lambda)$, the difference from the unrefined invariant with the Kähler variable shifted (§[-@sec-universal]). The fixed sector and the frozen states are defined in §[-@sec-index-setup], and the switching block in §[-@sec-split].

A $\sigma$-symmetric Laurent polynomial in $q_\ell^{1/2}, q_r^{1/2}$ with integer powers of $q_\ell$ is a polynomial in $G$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}[q_r^{\pm1/2}]$; writing it so is its *$G$-expansion* (Definition [-@def-c1]). Conversely, since $G$ and $q_r$ are $\sigma$-invariant, only $\sigma$-symmetric polynomials have a $G$-expansion. This is the refined counterpart of an unrefined fact: a Laurent polynomial in $q^{1/2}$ is a polynomial in $z = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}$ if and only if it is invariant under $q^{1/2} \to -q^{-1/2}$, i.e., its integer powers of $q$ are symmetric and its half-integer powers antisymmetric under $q \leftrightarrow 1/q$; the even powers of $z$ are the $c = 1$ part and the odd powers the $c = 2$ part of [@Marino09]. The expansion in genus is therefore conditional on a symmetry in both theories. The difference is that the unrefined symmetry holds for the invariants of [@Marino09], whereas $\sigma$-symmetry of the refined crosscap invariant holds only in the cases stated in §[-@sec-torus] and fails in those of §[-@sec-t34] and §[-@sec-sigmaasym].

## Refined $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ invariants and the dual Cauchy kernel {#sec-kernel}

In the $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ refined Chern--Simons theory of [@AgSc12], the Wilson loop in a representation $R$ is given by a Macdonald polynomial of type $D_N$, which is the specialization $K_R(x; q, t; 1, -1, q^{1/2}, -q^{1/2})$ of the Koornwinder polynomial [@Koornwinder92] (see [@vD96; @Sahi99]); the refined unknot $\dim_R$ of [@AgSc12] is its principal specialization $x = (1, t, \dots, t^{N-1})$ (checked for six representations with $|R| \le 3$, Appendix [A](#sec-app-code)). The dimension $\dim_R$ is not a Laurent polynomial in $t^N$: for $(2)$ it has the denominator $(1 - qt^{N-1})$ and for $(1,1)$ the denominator $(1 - qt^{2N-3})$; both cancel at $t = q$.

::: {#exr-naive}
## failure of the naive refinement; negative

If the construction of [@Marino09] is refined as it stands (bosonic Cauchy kernel, the factor $\tfrac12$, the sum over odd $d$), the poles in $U = t^N$ fail to cancel already for the two-box unknot. The composite $(1;\bar1)$ contributes only in the $p_1^2$ direction, whereas the poles of the $D_N$ representations $(2)$ and $(1,1)$ sit at different places ($t^N = t/q$ and $t^{2N} = t^3/q$). None of five choices of weights and three choices of basis removes the mismatch.
:::

We therefore use the dual Cauchy identity for Koornwinder polynomials [@Mimachi01], $$
\sum_{\mu \subseteq m^n} (-1)^{|\mu|} K_{m^n - \mu}(x; q, t)\, K_{\mu'}(y; t, q) = \prod_{i, j} x_i^{-1}(1 - x_i y_j)(1 - x_i y_j^{-1}),
$$ {#eq-mimachi} in which the holonomy side carries the $D_n$-type parameters $(\pm1, \pm q^{1/2})$ of [@AgSc12] and the probe side the parameters $(\pm 1, \pm t'^{1/2})$ for $(q', t') = (t, q)$. We read it as the Ooguri--Vafa kernel of the refined orientifold and set, for probe variables $Y = (y_1, y_2, \dots)$, $$
\tilde Z(Y) = \Bigl\langle \prod_{\alpha, i} (1 - y_\alpha x_i)(1 - y_\alpha x_i^{-1}) \Bigr\rangle_{\mathrm{SO}(2N)},\qquad
\log \tilde Z = \sum_{d \ge 1} \frac1d \sum_R f_R(q^d, t^d, \lambda^d)\, s_R(Y^d).
$$ {#eq-Z} Here $\langle F(x)\rangle_{\mathrm{SO}(2N)}$ is the linear map that expands a class function $F$ of the holonomy eigenvalues $x = (x_1, \dots, x_N)$ in Koornwinder polynomials $K_\mu(x; q, t; 1, -1, q^{1/2}, -q^{1/2})$ and replaces each term by the refined Chern--Simons knot invariant $W_\mu(K)$ (normalized as in §[-@sec-uniform]): $F = \sum_\mu c_\mu K_\mu(x)$ gives $\langle F\rangle := \sum_\mu c_\mu W_\mu(K)$. In the unrefined theory this is the path-integral expectation value of the Wilson loop, in which $x$ is integrated out. The sum in ([-@eq-Z]) runs over all $d$ ("all-$d$"), whereas in [@Marino09] it runs over odd $d$; the two are related in ([-@eq-odd]) below.

Since $(1 - x_iy_j^{-1}) = -x_iy_j^{-1}(1 - y_jx_i^{-1})$, the right-hand side of ([-@eq-mimachi]) with $n = N$ equals $(-1)^{Nm}(\prod_j y_j)^{-N}\prod_{i,j}(1 - y_jx_i)(1 - y_jx_i^{-1})$. Reading the identity with $m$ probes on the $y$ side and $N$ holonomies on the $x$ side, and relabeling the summation by the partition $m^N - \mu$ on the holonomy side (so that $(-1)^{|\mu|}$ becomes $(-1)^{Nm - |\mu|}$, which cancels the sign $(-1)^{Nm}$), the kernel of ([-@eq-Z]) is therefore $$
\begin{aligned}
\tilde Z(Y) &= \sum_{\mu \subseteq m^N} (-1)^{|\mu|}\, W_\mu(K)\, \hat K_{\mu'}(Y; t, q; U),\\
\hat K_{\mu'}(Y; t, q; U) &:= \Bigl(\prod_\alpha y_\alpha\Bigr)^N K_{N^m - \mu'}(Y; t, q; 1, -1, q^{1/2}, -q^{1/2}),\qquad U = t^N.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-Zexpand} The expansion runs over Koornwinder polynomials of type $(t, q)$ on the probe side; the complement in the rectangle $N^m$ multiplied by $(\prod y)^N$ is a virtual Koornwinder polynomial [@Rains05; @RW21], which depends on $N$ only through $U = t^N$. The kernel in ([-@eq-Z]) has no prefactor, so setting $y_{m+1} = 0$ reduces the $(m+1)$-probe kernel to the $m$-probe one; hence $\log\tilde Z$ is a well-defined symmetric function of $Y$, and the coefficient $f_R$ does not depend on the number of probes once $m \ge \ell(R)$.

The coefficients $f_R$ are extracted as follows. Write $\log\tilde Z = \sum_\rho L_\rho\, p_\rho(Y)$ in the power-sum basis. Since $s_R(Y^d) = \sum_\rho \chi_R(\rho) z_\rho^{-1} p_{d\rho}(Y)$, where $d\rho$ multiplies every part of $\rho$ by $d$, ([-@eq-Z]) gives $L_\rho = \sum_{d \mid \rho} d^{-1} z_{\rho/d}^{-1} f_{\rho/d}(q^d, t^d, \lambda^d)$ with the *power-sum components* $f_\rho := \sum_R \chi_R(\rho) f_R$, the sum over $d$ running over the common divisors of the parts of $\rho$. Möbius inversion in $d$ and the inverse character transform give $$
\frac{f_\rho(q,t,\lambda)}{z_\rho} = \sum_{d \mid \rho} \frac{\mu(d)}{d}\, L_{\rho/d}(q^d, t^d, \lambda^d),\qquad
f_R = \sum_\rho \frac{\chi_R(\rho)}{z_\rho}\, f_\rho ,
$$ {#eq-extract} with $\mu$ the Möbius function and $z_\rho$ the order of the centralizer of the cycle type $\rho$. We speak of the "$p_2$ direction" or "$p_1^2$ direction" of a two-box invariant for the components $f_{(2)}$ and $f_{(1,1)}$. In the actual computation (Appendix [A](#sec-app-code)) the kernel $\prod_{\alpha,i}(1 - y_\alpha x_i)(1 - y_\alpha x_i^{-1}) = \exp(-\sum_d p_d(Y)S_d(x)/d)$, $S_d(x) = \sum_i(x_i^d + x_i^{-d})$, is expanded in $K_\mu(x)$ by evaluating at the points $x = t^\rho q^\nu$, where $S_d(t^\rho q^\nu)$ is a rational function of $U$; this is why $U$ can be treated as a formal variable. The sign $(-1)^{|\mu|}$ in ([-@eq-Zexpand]) is the hallmark of a fermionic kernel. For the unknot $W_\mu = K_\mu(t^\rho) = \dim_\mu$ and ([-@eq-Zexpand]) reduces to the dual Cauchy identity evaluated at $x = t^\rho$, which is a product (§[-@sec-unknot]).

## Definition and computational scheme {#sec-procedure}

For the cover $\mathrm{U}(N_A)$, $N_A = 2N-1$, we define $f^{\mathrm{cov}}_R$ by the same kernel $\prod_{\alpha,i}(1 - y_\alpha x_i)(1 - y_\alpha x_i^{-1})$ with the same extraction ([-@eq-extract]). Since both $x$ and $x^{-1}$ enter, the expansion basis consists of Macdonald characters of composite representations $(\alpha; \bar\beta)$, and $\langle P_\alpha(x) P_\beta(x^{-1})\rangle$ is evaluated by decomposing into composite values and contraction terms (§[-@sec-generalN]). The part of the kernel with $|Y| \le 2$ is expressed through ordinary representations of $\mathrm{U}(N_A)$ and the adjoint composite $(1;\bar1)$; at degree three the composites $(2;\bar1)$ and $(1,1;\bar1)$ appear as well. In [@Marino09] the subtracted term is the $\mathrm{U}(N)$ invariant in composite representations evaluated at the $\mathrm{SO}(N)$ value of the Kähler variable; by the invariance under determinant shifts of Result [-@exr-uniform] this is the same as the $\mathrm{U}(N_A)$ invariant used here.

::: {#exm-cover}
## the cover

The oriented part of the orientifold theory is given by the A-type refined Chern--Simons invariants of the cover $\mathrm{U}(N_A)$ in ordinary and composite representations, in the uniform normalization of §[-@sec-uniform]. This is the refined version of the construction of [@Marino09]; for the fundamental representation it takes the explicit form of Hypothesis [-@exm-hg].
:::

::: {#def-crosscap}
## refined crosscap invariant

In the all-$d$ definition ([-@eq-Z]) we set $g_R = f_R - \tfrac12 f^{\mathrm{cov}}_R$, and the hatted (BPS-basis) invariant is $\hat g = M(q^{-1})^{-1} g$, where $$
M(x)_{RS} = \sum_{\mu \vdash |R|} \frac{\chi_R(\mu)\chi_S(\mu)}{z_\mu}\,\frac{\prod_i \bigl(x^{-\mu_i/2} - x^{\mu_i/2}\bigr)}{x^{-1/2} - x^{1/2}} ,
$$ {#eq-M} with a single denominator for the whole product. In the power-sum basis $M(x)$ is diagonal with entries $\prod_i(x^{-\mu_i/2} - x^{\mu_i/2})/(x^{-1/2} - x^{1/2})$; at $x = q^{-1}$ these are $z_q$ for $\mu = (1,1)$ and $z_q^+$ for $\mu = (2)$, and in the Schur basis $(\ydB, \ydAA)$ $$
M(q^{-1}) = \begin{pmatrix} q^{1/2} & -q^{-1/2} \\ -q^{-1/2} & q^{1/2} \end{pmatrix},\qquad
M(q^{-1})^{-1} = \frac{1}{q - q^{-1}}\begin{pmatrix} q^{1/2} & q^{-1/2} \\ q^{-1/2} & q^{1/2} \end{pmatrix}.
$$ {#eq-M2} $M(x)$ is the matrix $M(x)$ of [@KN17]; it equals the reformulation matrix of [@Marino09], written with $t_M = x^{-1/2}$ and divided by the one-box factor $t_M - t_M^{-1}$ so that $M_{\ydA\ydA} = 1$.
:::

The choice of $M(q^{-1})$ is forced by the Hopf link: with $M(t)$ or $M(t^{-1})$ in its place the Hopf link invariants are not Laurent polynomials, and $M(q)$ exchanges $R \leftrightarrow R^T$. The two formulations of [@KN17] (the $q$-side with the Macdonald Cauchy kernel and $M(t)$, the $t$-side with the dual Cauchy kernel and $M(q^{-1})$) give the same hatted invariants with two boxes (Result [-@exr-largeN]).

The invariant $g_R$ is computed in three steps: $f_R$ from the $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ invariants $W^{\mathrm{SO}}_\mu$ ($|\mu| \le |R|$, type $D_N$) by ([-@eq-Z]) and ([-@eq-extract]); $f^{\mathrm{cov}}_R$ from the A-type invariants of the cover (ordinary representations, the adjoint, and for three boxes $(2;\bar1), (1,1;\bar1)$ with contraction terms) in the same way; and $g_R = f_R - \tfrac12 f^{\mathrm{cov}}_R$, hatted with $M(q^{-1})^{-1}$. The invariant $f_R$ closes on the $\mathrm{SO}$ side and $f^{\mathrm{cov}}_R$ contains no $\mathrm{SO}$ data. Why the difference $g$, and not $f$ itself, is the quantity with a BPS expansion is explained in §[-@sec-alld]. Writing the cover with two sets of probes, brane ($Y$) and image ($Y'$), $f^{\mathrm{cov}}$ splits into a brane--brane part (the invariant of [@KN17] itself) and a brane--image part (the connected part of the composites), see §[-@sec-cover].

## Normalization {#sec-uniform}

The input $\mathrm{U}(n)$ refined invariants, normalized by conditions (N1) and (N2) of [@KN17], change by powers of $(q/t)$ under determinant shifts and charge conjugation. With $\delta$ the Seifert genus (§[-@sec-variables]) we set $$
W_R = (t/q)^{\delta |R|/2}\, \mathcal{R}_R\, P_R(t^\rho),
$$ {#eq-uniform} where $\mathcal{R}_R$ is the reduced invariant (the refined invariant divided by that of the unknot, computed in §[-@sec-generalN] from DAHA-Jones polynomials) and $P_R(t^\rho)$ the Macdonald dimension. Throughout, $P_R(t^\rho)$ denotes the principal specialization of the Macdonald polynomial of $\mathrm{U}(n)$, and $K_R(t^\rho) = \dim_R$ that of the $D_N$ Koornwinder polynomial of §[-@sec-kernel]; on the $\mathrm{SO}$ side the reduced invariant is $\mathcal{R}_R = W_R/K_R(t^\rho)$, with no factor $(t/q)^{\delta|R|/2}$ (Result [-@exr-monomial]).

::: {#exr-uniform}
The normalization ([-@eq-uniform]) has the following properties. The invariant $W$ is exactly invariant under the determinant shift $R \to R + 1^n$ and under charge conjugation; this was checked for 16 pairs for the trefoil ($\mathrm{U}(2)$--$\mathrm{U}(5)$), 13 pairs each for $T(2,5)$ and $T(2,7)$, and seven double-twist knots. At fixed $N$ ($N = 2, 3$, $|R| \le 3$), fixing the framing monomial by requiring the cancellation of $N$-dependent poles and the value $1$ at $t = q$ gives the monomial $1$ on both the $\mathrm{SO}$ side and the cover side ($T(2,3), T(2,5), T(2,7)$), and within the family $(t/q)^{\beta/2}$ the exponent $\beta$ is unique. The DAHA-Jones polynomials (vertical framing) agree with $W$ up to powers of the framing eigenvalue (§[-@sec-generalN]). At $t = q$ the normalization is the standard framing of [@Marino09].
:::

::: {#exm-framing}
The uniform normalization ([-@eq-uniform]) is the normalization at framing zero.
:::

The normalization of the inputs involves several freedoms. Table [-@tbl-norm] lists each of them, how it was fixed, and which checks were made afterwards and did not enter the fixing. The number of fitted quantities is small (one monomial per knot and side, the exponent $\delta$, and the constant $\mathsf{c}_K$ of ([-@eq-Mb])), while the subsequent checks involve all coefficients of the invariants at many values of $N$ and of the representation; in particular the integrality of $g_R$ at general $N$ (§[-@sec-generalN]) is not used anywhere in the fixing.

## The unknot {#sec-unknot}

::: {#prp-unknot}
For the unknot, $f_{10} = (1 - t^N)(t^N + t)/(t^N(t-1))$ and $f_{a0} = 0$ for $a \ge 2$ (the first index counts probes on the knot, the second on a second component, cf. §[-@sec-hopf]). In terms of $\lambda$, $$
f_{10} = -1 - \frac{\lambda - \lambda^{-1}}{t^{1/2} - t^{-1/2}},
$$ {#eq-f10} and the product formula is $\prod_j (y_j; t)_\infty (t y_j/U; t)_\infty / \bigl((U y_j; t)_\infty (t y_j; t)_\infty\bigr)$.
:::

::: {.proof}
At $x = t^\rho$, $x_k = t^{N-k}$, the kernel is $\prod_j\prod_{k=1}^{N}(1 - t^{N-k}y_j)(1 - t^{k-N}y_j)$; take the logarithm and apply ([-@eq-extract]).
:::

The right-hand side of ([-@eq-f10]) is the sum of the unknot of [@Marino09], $(\lambda - \lambda^{-1})/z$, and the crosscap term $-1$. In our conventions $g_{\ydA}$ is minus the mirror of the crosscap invariant of [@Marino09] (Result [-@exr-marino]), so $-1$ corresponds to the value $g_{\ydA} = 1$ of [@Marino09] for the unknot. Neither the factor $\tfrac12$ nor the restriction to odd $d$ is needed to obtain the product formula.

# The orientifold index and the all-$d$ structure {#sec-index}

## Setup {#sec-index-setup}

Following §3 of [@AgSc12], M-theory on $\mathcal{X} \times \mathrm{TN} \times S^1$, with $\mathcal X$ the resolved conifold, is twisted by $(q, t)$. The orientifold action $\tilde I$ is the composition of an antiholomorphic involution $I$ of $\mathcal X$ with $z_2 \to -z_2$ in spacetime. The probe of a knot $K$ is an M5-brane extended along the $z_2$ plane (a $t$-brane: the open-string denominator is $1/(1-t)$). On the cover there are two of them, $L_K$ and its image $I(L_K)$; see Figure [-@fig-orientifold]. The space of one-particle states on the cover is $H_1 = H_{\mathrm{int}} \otimes F_{z_2}$, where $F_{z_2}$ consists of the modes $t^l$, $l \ge 0$, in the $z_2$ direction, on which $\tilde I$ acts by $(-1)^l$. A *sector* of the generating function is labeled by the numbers of boxes (total windings) on $L_K$ and on $I(L_K)$; a sector is *fixed* when $\tilde I$ maps it to itself, i.e., when the two numbers are equal. States that exist only in the quotient, frozen at $z_2 = 0$ and wrapped on non-orientable surfaces, are called *frozen states*.

![The cover with the brane $L_K$ and its image $I(L_K)$, and the three classes of one-particle states of Hypothesis [-@exm-classes]: pairs exchanged by $\tilde I$, states invariant under $\tilde I$ (in fixed sectors, with equal numbers of boundaries on $L_K$ and $I(L_K)$), and frozen states, whose world-sheets are quotients of surfaces connecting $L_K$ to $I(L_K)$ (an annulus becomes a Möbius strip).](fig1.svg){#fig-orientifold}

::: {#exm-classes}
## classification of one-particle states

The one-particle states of the quotient are the $\tilde I$-orbits on the cover and fall into three classes: (a) pairs $\{\psi, \tilde I\psi\}$ exchanged by $\tilde I$, carrying the full tower of modes; (b) invariant states $\tilde I\psi = \varepsilon\psi$ ($\varepsilon = \pm 1$), carrying only the modes with $(-1)^l\varepsilon = 1$; and (c) frozen states, carrying no tower of modes. This is the classification underlying the product formula (3.13) of [@AgSc12] for closed strings, extrapolated to open strings.
:::

## All-$d$ structure {#sec-alld}

::: {#prp-alld}
Under Hypothesis [-@exm-classes], writing $\omega_\psi$ for the charge (the monomial in $q, t, \lambda$) of a state $\psi$, $$
g = f - \tfrac12 f^{\mathrm{cov}} = \frac12\,\frac{E}{1+t} + C,\qquad E = \sum_{\text{invariant}} \varepsilon_\psi\, \omega_\psi,\qquad C = \sum_{\text{frozen}} \omega_\psi .
$$ {#eq-alld}
:::

::: {.proof}
The index of the cover is $f^{\mathrm{cov}} = \sum_{\text{pairs}} 2\omega/(1-t) + \sum_{\text{invariant}} \omega/(1-t)$, that of the quotient is $f = \sum_{\text{pairs}} \omega/(1-t) + \sum_{\text{invariant}} \omega \sum_{(-1)^l\varepsilon = 1} t^l + \sum_{\text{frozen}} \omega$. Substitute $\sum_{(-1)^l\varepsilon = 1} t^l = \tfrac12[1/(1-t) + \varepsilon/(1+t)]$.
:::

The proof shows why the $\mathrm{SO}$ free energy $f$ itself is not the object to expand in BPS numbers. It is a superposition of three kinds of states whose towers of modes differ: pairs carry the full tower $1/(1-t)$, invariant states only the modes of one parity, and frozen states no tower. No single prefactor turns $f$ into a count of states; accordingly $f_R$ has no $N$-dependent poles but is not a Laurent polynomial: its denominator is a monomial times $(1-t)$ for one box and $(1-t)(1+t)$ for two boxes, with integer numerator (computed for the trefoil and $T(2,5)$). Subtracting $\tfrac12 f^{\mathrm{cov}}$ removes the pairs and the $1/(1-t)$ half of the invariant states, which belong to the oriented theory and contain no new information (the brane--brane part is the invariant of [@KN17], §[-@sec-split]), and leaves the two terms of ([-@eq-alld]), each with a definite meaning. At $t = q$ this is the subtraction of [@Marino09], whose integrality conjecture concerns $g$ and not the Kauffman invariant itself.

::: {#rem-Esector}
*Remark 9*. Invariant states exist only in fixed sectors; hence $E$ appears only there. If $\tilde I$ acts as the exchange of brane and image, its trace enters the power-sum basis in the $p_2$-type direction (the Adams operation $\psi^2$), and $E_{\ydB} = -E_{\ydAA}$. The latter is consistent with the computations for the Hopf link (Result [-@exr-E22]) and for knots with two boxes (Result [-@exr-largeN]).
:::

::: {#rem-trace}
*Remark 10* (trace form). Equation ([-@eq-alld]) can be written as a trace: $f = \mathrm{Tr}_{H_1^{\mathrm{cov}}}(P_+\cdot) + C$ with the projection $P_+ = \tfrac12(1 + \tilde I)$, and $\mathrm{Tr}(\tilde I\cdot) = \sum_{\text{invariant}}\varepsilon\omega\sum_l(-t)^l = E/(1+t)$, so $g = \tfrac12\mathrm{Tr}_{H_1^{\mathrm{cov}}}(\tilde I\cdot) + C$. Thus $E$ is a twisted trace over the states of the cover and $C$ the contribution of states existing only in the quotient. This is the $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ analog of the two expressions given in [@Witten11] (§3.4 there) for the Chern--Simons partition function of a non-simply-laced group: a trace with an outer automorphism inserted over the larger theory, and an ordinary trace over the fixed theory; the $D$-type $(2,0)$ theory arises there from M5-branes on $\mathcal X/\mathbb{Z}_2$ (§5.1.4 of [@Witten11], Appendix A of [@AgSc12]), which is the five-brane origin of $\tilde I$. The ambiguity of Proposition [-@prp-EC] below is the ambiguity in splitting one number into these two expressions.
:::

## Action of $\tilde I$ on boundary zero modes {#sec-boundary}

In §3.2 of [@KN17], a holomorphic curve with $h$ boundaries carries boundary zero modes $d\theta_i$, $i = 1, \dots, h$, with the constraint $\sum_i d\theta_i = 0$; they span hook representations, and in the $t$-brane formulation each independent mode contributes a factor $(1 - q^{-1})$, which we normalize by $q^{1/2}$ to $z_q$.

::: {#prp-boundary}
Assume the boundary zero mode picture of [@KN17] and let $\tilde I$ exchange the boundaries on $L_K$ with those on $I(L_K)$. A $\tilde I$-invariant curve lies in a fixed sector and has the same number $n$ of boundaries on $L_K$ and on $I(L_K)$, exchanged in pairs $(\theta_i, \theta_i')$. The sum $d\theta_i + d\theta_i'$ is $\tilde I$-even and the difference $d\theta_i - d\theta_i'$ is $\tilde I$-odd; the constraint $\sum d\theta = 0$ removes one even mode. In the trace with $\tilde I$ inserted an odd mode contributes $(1 + q^{-1})$ instead of $(1 - q^{-1})$. Hence $$
\text{boundary factor of } E = z_q^{\,n-1}(z_q^+)^{\,n},\qquad
\text{boundary factor of } \Phi:= (1-t)f^{\mathrm{cov}}\big|_{\text{fixed sector}} = z_q^{\,2n-1}.
$$ {#eq-boundary}
:::

::: {.proof}
A curve whose numbers of boxes on $L_K$ and $I(L_K)$ differ is mapped by $\tilde I$ to a different sector and cannot be invariant; for an invariant curve $\tilde I$ maps boundaries on $L_K$ bijectively to boundaries on $I(L_K)$. Multiply $n-1$ even factors $(1 - q^{-1})$ and $n$ odd factors $(1 + q^{-1})$ for $E$, and $2n - 1$ factors $(1 - q^{-1})$ for $\Phi$; the normalization by $q^{1/2}$ turns them into $z_q$ and $z_q^+$.
:::

The predictions are compared with the computations in Result [-@exr-boundary]. What remains unknown is the action of $\tilde I$ on the moduli part $H^*(\mathcal{M}_{g,h,\beta})$, i.e., the sign $\varepsilon$ for each $\beta$.

## The $E$--$C$ ambiguity and the conditions fixing $E$ {#sec-Econd}

::: {#prp-EC}
For any integer Laurent polynomial $X$, the replacement $E \to E + 2(1+t)X$, $C \to C - X$ leaves $g$ unchanged. Hence $g$ determines only the class of $E$ modulo $2(1+t)$; in particular $E$ itself is not determined, while $E(-1) = [2(1+t)g]_{t=-1}$ is.
:::

::: {.proof}
$\tfrac12 \cdot 2(1+t)X/(1+t) = X$, so the change of $E$ is compensated by that of $C$. In terms of states, the following two configurations are indistinguishable in both $f$ and $f^{\mathrm{cov}}$: a frozen state $\omega$ together with two pairs exchanged by $\tilde I$, one of charge $\omega$ and one of charge $\omega t$; and four invariant states $\omega, \omega, \omega t, \omega t$ with $\varepsilon = +1$. Both contribute $2(\omega + \omega t)/(1-t)$ to $f^{\mathrm{cov}}$ and $2\omega/(1-t)$ to $f$.
:::

::: {#cor-Efree}
The $p_1^n$ directions of the power-sum basis and the sectors with an odd number of boxes (where $E = 0$) are independent of $E$. In these directions positivity can be tested independently of the $E$ ambiguity.
:::

The definition $g^{\mathrm{odd}}$ of [@Marino09] with $\sum_{d\ \mathrm{odd}}$ is related to the all-$d$ definition as follows. Writing the oriented part with all $d$ and the crosscap part with odd $d$ only, as in [@Marino09], and comparing with ([-@eq-Z]), the terms with even $d$ of the all-$d$ expansion are accounted for by the Adams operation on $g^{\mathrm{odd}}$: $$
g_{ab} = g^{\mathrm{odd}}_{ab} - \tfrac12 g^{\mathrm{odd}}_{a/2, b/2}(x^2),
$$ {#eq-odd} where $(x^2)$ denotes the Adams operation $\psi^2$ on all variables and the second term is present only when $a, b$ are both even (for a knot, only in the $p_2$-type directions). The factor $4(1+t)(1+t^2)$ appearing in the denominators of the $\sum_{d\,\mathrm{odd}}$ definition for the Hopf link cancels in the all-$d$ definition (Result [-@exr-hopfdenom]).

Two conditions on $E$ are used throughout the paper. The first, which we call (E1), is $E|_{t=-1} = [2(1+t)g]_{t=-1}$; it is derived in Proposition [-@prp-EC]. The second, (E2), states that at $t = q$ the frozen sum $C$ equals the odd-$d$ crosscap invariant $g^{\mathrm{odd}}$ of [@Marino09] with its unknot value subtracted; it is stated as Hypothesis [-@exm-E2].

::: {#exm-E2}
At $t = q$ the frozen states reproduce the crosscap BPS invariants of [@Marino09], and the $\tilde I$-invariant states account for the Adams correction in ([-@eq-odd]). The constant $-1$ of the unknot ([-@eq-f10]) is excluded from the Adams correction: for the unknot $g_{a0} = 0$ for $a \ge 2$, so $E = C = 0$ there, and the unknot value of $g^{\mathrm{odd}}$ ($-\tfrac12$ in the $p_2$ direction) is subtracted from $C$, as in the comparison with [@Marino09] in Result [-@exr-marino].
:::

Hypothesis [-@exm-E2] fixes the ambiguity of Proposition [-@prp-EC] at $t = q$. By ([-@eq-alld]) and ([-@eq-odd]), in a sector $(a,b)$ with $a, b$ even it reads $E|_{t=q} = -(1+q)\,\psi^2 g^{\mathrm{odd}}_{a/2,b/2}$; for the two-box $p_2$ direction of a knot, $E|_{t=q} = -(1+q)\,\psi^2(g_{\ydA} + 1)$, where $+1$ is the exclusion of the unknot constant stated in Hypothesis [-@exm-E2]. When $E$ is determined by (E1) and (E2) in this paper, it is by solving these conditions, together with the parity and bound constraints of Appendix [A.4](#sec-app-ilp), as an integer linear program.

For closed strings the situation is simpler. There are only two kinds of states, $\mathbb{P}^1$ (an invariant state with $\varepsilon = +1$) and $\mathbb{RP}^2$ (a frozen state), with no cancellation between them, so $E$ and $C$ are unique and ([-@eq-alld]) can be tested directly. The $D_N$ product formula of the partition function reproduces the three terms of the free energy of [@AgSc12], which are the closed-string version of ([-@eq-alld]), and the "Klein bottle" term of [@AM22] is a rearrangement of the frozen-state term; see Appendix [B](#sec-app-closed). The ambiguity of Proposition [-@prp-EC] first arises for open strings.

# Unknot and Hopf link {#sec-hopf}

## Hopf link

We attach one probe to each component (variables $y_1$, $y_2$) and set $f_{ab} = \sum_{d | (a,b)} (\mu(d)/d)\, L_{a/d, b/d}(q^d, t^d, \lambda^d)$, where $L_{ab}$ is the coefficient of $y_1^a y_2^b$ in $\log\tilde Z$ (this is ([-@eq-extract]) for one probe per component). The one-probe computation uses a closed form for the Askey--Wilson coefficients which has not been proved; it is stated as Conjecture [-@cnj-c2j] in Appendix [A.3](#sec-app-virtual), and its consequences were checked against the direct computation at $N = 3, \dots, 8$.

::: {#exr-hopf}
For $a, b \le 4$ one has $f_{ab} \in \dfrac{1 - q}{1 - t}\,\mathbb{Z}[q^\pm, t^\pm, (t^N)^\pm]$; when $a, b$ are both even the denominator is $1 - t^2$. The same integrality holds in the Schur basis $f_{R,b}$ with infinitely many probes on the first component ($|R| \le 4$, $b \le 2$), whereas in a naive Macdonald basis extra denominators such as $(1 - qt)$ appear. Moreover, $f_{11} = -f_{10}\, z_q(\tilde\lambda- \tilde\lambda^{-1})$ and $f_{1b} = f_{11}\,\chi_{b-1}(t^{N-1})$ with $\chi_m(x) = x^m + x^{m-2} + \dots + x^{-m}$. At $t = q$ this agrees with $\hat g_{\ydA,\ydA} = z(\lambda - \lambda^{-1})$ of [@Marino09] up to the sign and the unknot factor.
:::

::: {#exr-hopfdenom}
For $a, b \le 4$ the denominators of the all-$d$ invariants $g_{ab}$ are $2(1+t)\times$ a monomial in the (even, even) sectors and monomials otherwise.
:::

After refinement the Kähler variable is shifted to $\tilde\lambda= \lambda (q/t)^{1/2}$. This may be the open-string version of the quantum shift of the Kähler variable in [@AM22], but the ratio of shifts does not match the closed-string one. For closed strings the ratio of charges of frozen and oriented states is $x^2/Q_0 = q_r^{-1}$ (conventions of [@AgSc12], Appendix [B](#sec-app-closed)), whereas for open strings the ratio of the crosscap variable $\tilde\lambda^2$ to the cover variable $\boldsymbol{a}_{\mathrm{KN}}^2 = \lambda^2q_r^{-1}$ is $q_r^{3}$. Since the correspondence of open and closed variables ($\lambda^2$ or $\lambda^{-2}$ with $Q$) and the open-string normalization are not yet fixed, we leave this comparison open.

## Crosscap part

On the cover we use the Hopf link of $\mathrm{U}(N_A)$ refined Chern--Simons theory in composite representations: $\tfrac12 f^{\mathrm{cov}}_{10} = -(\lambda - \lambda^{-1})/z_t$ and $\tfrac12 f^{\mathrm{cov}}_{11} = (\lambda - \lambda^{-1})(\tilde\lambda- \tilde\lambda^{-1})z_q/z_t$.

::: {#exr-hopfg}
For the crosscap part of the Hopf link, $g_{1b} = z_q(\tilde\lambda- \tilde\lambda^{-1})\,\chi_{b-1}(\tilde\lambda/q^{1/2})$ for $b \le 4$, so that $t$ enters only through $\tilde\lambda$. The hatted invariant $\hat g_{R,\ydA}$ ($|R| \le 4$) is an integer Laurent polynomial: it is $(-1)^d z_q(\tilde\lambda- \tilde\lambda^{-1})\tilde\lambda^{2d-n+1}$ for hooks $R = (n-d, 1^d)$ and $0$ otherwise. At $t = q$ this agrees with $\hat g_{\ydB,\ydA} = z(\lambda^2 - 1)$, $\hat g_{\ydAA,\ydA} = z(\lambda^{-2} - 1)$ of [@Marino09] up to $R \leftrightarrow R^T$ and an overall sign.
:::

## Determination of $E_{22}$ and $E_{24}$ {#sec-E22}

When the probes of both components are split into an $x$ side (brane) and a $1/x$ side (image), the sector $(a,b) = (2,2)$ has a fixed subsector with one brane box and one image box on each component, hence $n = 2$ pairs of boundaries in the sense of Proposition [-@prp-boundary]; similarly for $(2,4)$. The index of the cover restricted to this fixed sector is the sum $\Phi$ over its states. Write $E = \Phi- 2\Phi_-$, with $\Phi_-$ the sum over the states with $\tilde I$-eigenvalue $-1$.

::: {#exm-QP}
The coefficients of the monomials of $\Phi$ are numbers of states, and $0 \le (\Phi_-)_\omega/\Phi_\omega \le 1$ for each monomial $\omega$.
:::

For knots the signs of $\Phi$ are mixed and Hypothesis [-@exm-QP] cannot be used (§[-@sec-EC]).

::: {#exr-E22}
Under Hypothesis [-@exm-QP], (E1) and (E2), solved as an integer program (Appendix [A.4](#sec-app-ilp)), $$
E_{22} = -z_q (z_q^+)^2(\tilde\lambda- \tilde\lambda^{-1})(t q^{-1/2}\tilde\lambda+ q^{1/2}\tilde\lambda^{-1})\ \ (\text{unique}),\qquad
E_{24} = E_{22}\,(\tilde\lambda^2/q + q/\tilde\lambda^2)\ \ (\text{unique}).
$$ {#eq-E22} For $(4,4)$ a solution exists but is not unique (164 of the 180 monomials of the fixed sector are free). With many probes on the first component, $\tilde I$ acts as "exchange of the fixed sector plus Adams operation" and $E_{R,S} = \sum_{\rho, \sigma\vdash 2} c^R_{2;\rho}c^S_{2;\sigma}\,\varepsilon_{\rho\sigma}$, where $c^R_{2;\rho}$ are the coefficients of the Adams operation $\psi^2 s_\rho$ expanded in Schur functions $s_R$. This was checked for the ten sectors $(R, S)$ with $|R| \in \{2, 4\}$, $|S| = 2$ in which the refined part is non-zero (Result [-@exr-hopfC]), and at $t = -1$ for all $|R| = |S| = 4$ (25 pairs): solving $\varepsilon_{\rho\sigma}(-1)$ from 4 of the 25 pairs, the remaining 21 agree.
:::

Compared with $\Phi_{22} = z_q^3(\tilde\lambda- \tilde\lambda^{-1})(tq^{-1/2}\tilde\lambda- q^{1/2}\tilde\lambda^{-1})$, $E_{22}$ replaces the difference factor $z_q^2$ by the sum factor $-(z_q^+)^2$ and flips the sign in the second factor. This is the form of a twisted trace of $\tilde I$, which we apply to knots in §[-@sec-EC].

::: {#exr-hopfC}
With many probes on the first component ($|R| \le 4$) and two boxes on the second ($|S| \le 2$), split $\hat C_{R,S} = M(q^{-1})^{-1}\,(g - \tfrac12E/(1+t))\,M(q^{-1})^{-1\,T}$ into the $t = q$ part (written in $\tilde\lambda$) and the refined part. Among the fourteen components with $|R| \in \{2,4\}$, $|S| = 2$, the refined part vanishes for $\hat C_{(2),(1,1)}$ and $\hat C_{(1,1),(2)}$ and for two more, leaving ten non-trivial components. In all ten the refined part is divisible by $(\tilde\lambda^2 - q)(q - t)$, which in bold variables is $\boldsymbol{t}^2(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)\cdot\boldsymbol{q}^2(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)$, and the $t = q$ part has aligned signs in each power of $\tilde\lambda$ in all components. The quotient of the refined part is aligned in 8 of the 10 components; in the transposed pair $\hat C_{(3,1),(1,1)}$, $\hat C_{(2,1,1),(2)}$ a factor $q^{1/2}(1-t)$ enters the $\tilde\lambda^2$ block and breaks the alignment.
:::

## Boundary factors

:::: {#exr-boundary}
The boundary factors of Proposition [-@prp-boundary] compare with the computations as follows.

::: center
  object                                   $n$   boundary factor of $E$   boundary factor of $\Phi$
  ---------------------------------------- ----- ------------------------ ---------------------------
  Hopf $(2,2)$, $(2,4)$                    2     $z_q(z_q^+)^2$           $z_q^3$
  unknot with framing $\mathsf f = 2, 4$   1     $z_q^+$                  $z_q$
  $T(2,3)$, $T(2,5)$, $p_2$ direction      1     $z_q^+$                  $z_q$
:::

For the Hopf link and the framed unknot $E$ is determined independently (Result [-@exr-E22] and Result [-@exr-framed]) and its boundary factor is read off. For knots $E$ is determined only modulo $2(1+t)$, so the statement is one of consistency: the integer programs of §[-@sec-EC] have solutions only with the boundary factor $z_q^+$, and the $E$ constructed in §[-@sec-principle] has this factor.
::::

# The sign property for torus knots in the fundamental representation {#sec-torus}

## Input and the $h/g$ decomposition

The input is the general formula of §6 of [@AgSc12] for $T(2,2m+1)$ in the fundamental representation (normalized by the unknot); for $m = 1$ it is (6.15) there. Under the identifications $\mathrm{SO}(4) = \mathrm{SU}(2)^2$ and $\mathrm{SO}(6) = \mathrm{SU}(4)$, (6.15) agrees with the $\mathrm{U}(n)$ values obtained from the construction of [@GN13] (checked exactly at two rational points). At $t = q$ it agrees with the mirror image of the Kauffman polynomial of [@Marino09] up to a framing monomial.

::: {#exm-hg}
## $h/g$ decomposition

Write $f_{\ydA}(K) = -W_{\mathrm{SO}}(K) = -\tfrac12 h_{\ydA} + g_{\ydA}$, i.e., $\tfrac12 f^{\mathrm{cov}}_{\ydA} = -\tfrac12 h_{\ydA}$, with the cover part $$
\tfrac12 h_{\ydA} = \mathcal{P}(\boldsymbol{a}_{\mathrm{KN}}, \boldsymbol{q}, \boldsymbol{t})\,\frac{\lambda - \lambda^{-1}}{\boldsymbol{q}- \boldsymbol{q}^{-1}},\qquad \boldsymbol{a}_{\mathrm{KN}}^2 = a\,(t/q)^{1/2},
$$ {#eq-hg} where $\mathcal P$ is the superpolynomial of [@DGR05], i.e., the A-type refined Chern--Simons invariant in the fundamental representation [@AgSh11]. This is Hypothesis [-@exm-cover] for the fundamental representation.
:::

::: {#exr-monomial}
For $m = 1, \dots, 5$ we searched for monomials $\pm q^{k_1/2} t^{k_2/2} (t^N)^{k_3}$ for which $g_{\ydA}$ becomes a Laurent polynomial. The only solutions have $k_3 = -2(2m+1)$ and $k_1 = -(3m+2)$; $k_2$ is fixed uniquely to $k_2 = 7m+4$ by requiring the $t = q$ limit to have the form of a Kauffman polynomial. The monomial is therefore $T_{\ydA}^{-2(2m+1)}(q/t)^{\delta/2}$ with $T_{\ydA} = q^{1/2}t^{N-1}$ and $\delta = m$. In the uniform normalization the extra $(q/t)^{\delta/2}$ moves to the cover, and the $\mathrm{SO}$ monomial is exactly $T_{\ydA}^{-2(2m+1)}$ (full agreement with the data at fixed $N = 2, 3$ for $m \le 3$).
:::

The same factor $\sqrt{q/t}$ appears for the $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ trefoil in [@AgSh11].

## Results, with the trefoil as an example

Write $g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA} = -(t/q)^{\delta/2} g_{\ydA}$ for the crosscap part in the uniform normalization, with the sign chosen so that $g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA} = W_{\mathrm{SO}} - \tfrac12 h_{\ydA}$ and the unknot has $g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA} = +1$ (in the convention of §[-@sec-setup] the unknot has $g_{\ydA} = -1$, Proposition [-@prp-unknot]). For the trefoil ($m = 1$) it has eleven terms, $$
\begin{aligned}
g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA}(T(2,3)) ={}& \boldsymbol{a}^{-6}\boldsymbol{t}^{-4} + \boldsymbol{a}^{-5}(\boldsymbol{q}\boldsymbol{t}^{-2} - \boldsymbol{q}\boldsymbol{t}^{-4}) + \boldsymbol{a}^{-4}(-\boldsymbol{q}^{2}\boldsymbol{t}^{-2} - \boldsymbol{t}^{-2} - \boldsymbol{q}^{-2}\boldsymbol{t}^{-4})\\
&+ \boldsymbol{a}^{-3}(-\boldsymbol{q}^{-1}\boldsymbol{t}^{-2} + \boldsymbol{q}^{-1}\boldsymbol{t}^{-4}) + \boldsymbol{a}^{-2}(\boldsymbol{q}^{2} + \boldsymbol{t}^{-2} + \boldsymbol{q}^{-2}\boldsymbol{t}^{-2}),
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-trefoil1} whose odd powers of $\boldsymbol{a}$ combine to $-(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)\,\boldsymbol{a}^{-5}\boldsymbol{q}^{-1}\boldsymbol{t}^{-4}$ (the $c = 2$ part) and whose even powers (the $c = 1$ part) have, in the variables $G, q_r$, the blocks $\lambda^{-6}$: $q_r^{-4}$; $\lambda^{-4}$: $-q_r^{-4}(Gq_r+ 2q_r^2 + 1)$; $\lambda^{-2}$: $q_r^{-2}(Gq_r+ q_r^2 + 2)$, each with a common sign (Figure [-@fig-blocks]).

::: {#def-c12}
For the fundamental representation the $c = 2$ part of $g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA}$ is the part with odd powers of $\boldsymbol{a}$ and the $c = 1$ part the part with even powers of $\boldsymbol{a}$. By the parity (P) of Result [-@exr-torus] the $c = 1$ part is also the part with integer powers of $q_\ell$; at $t = q$ the two parts reduce to the $c = 1$ and $c = 2$ contributions of [@Marino09].
:::

![The $G$-expansion of the $c = 1$ part of $g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA}$ for the trefoil: the coefficients $N^{c=1}_{g,\beta,J}$ of Definition [-@def-c1], arranged by $\lambda^\beta$ block (columns) and power of $G$ (rows); the powers of $q_r$ are suppressed. Each column has a common sign (light: positive, dark: negative), which is the sign property of Conjecture [-@cnj-criterion]. For $m \ge 2$ the intermediate columns are $(\boldsymbol{t}^2-1)$ times such a column.](fig2.svg){#fig-blocks}

::: {#exr-torus}
For $m = 1, \dots, 5$, $g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA}$ is an integer Laurent polynomial (with 11, 27, 49, 77, 111 terms) with the following properties.

- \(N\) $g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA} = 1$ at the $\mathrm{SO}(2)$ point $\boldsymbol{a}^2 = \boldsymbol{q}^2$ ($\lambda^2 = t$).

- \(P\) It is invariant under $\boldsymbol{t}\to -\boldsymbol{t}$.

- ($c{=}2$) The $c = 2$ part is $$
    -(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)\,\boldsymbol{a}^{-(4m+1)}\boldsymbol{q}^{-(2m-1)}\boldsymbol{t}^{-4m}\,\Pi_m,\qquad
  \Pi_m = \sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\boldsymbol{a}^{2j}\boldsymbol{q}^{2(m-1-j)}\boldsymbol{t}^{2j}\sum_{i=0}^{j}(\boldsymbol{q}^4\boldsymbol{t}^2)^i ,
  $$ {#eq-Pim} where $\Pi_m$ has $m(m+1)/2$ terms, all with coefficient $+1$.

- ($c{=}1$) The $c = 1$ part is $\sigma$-symmetric and is a polynomial in $G$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}[q_r^{\pm1}]$. Each $\lambda^\beta$ block is of one of four kinds: the block $\lambda^{-(4m+2)}$ is a positive monomial; the blocks $\lambda^{-4m}, \dots, \lambda^{-(2m+4)}$ (absent for $m = 1$) are $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)\times$ a block with positive coefficients; the block $\lambda^{-(2m+2)}$ has all coefficients negative; and the block $\lambda^{-2m}$ has all coefficients positive.
:::

::: {#cnj-Pim}
The closed form ([-@eq-Pim]) of the $c = 2$ part holds for all $m$. (It was guessed from $m \le 3$ and confirmed for $m = 4, 5$.)
:::

At $t = q$ the $c = 2$ part vanishes, consistent with the vanishing of the unrefined $c = 2$ invariants for torus knots in the fundamental representation. The values for $m = 1, 2, 3$ are listed in Appendix [D.1](#sec-app-torus).

## The sign property {#sec-criterion}

The unrefined crosscap BPS numbers are integers whose sign depends on $\beta$ (e.g., $\hat g_{\ydA,\ydA} = z(\lambda - \lambda^{-1})$ for the Hopf link in [@Marino09]). After refinement one expects positivity, which we formulate as follows: in each $\lambda^\beta$ block the coefficients have a common sign, equal to the unrefined sign $\varepsilon_\beta$ whenever the block survives at $t = q$. The expansion in $G$ used below exists only when the $c = 1$ part is $\sigma$-symmetric (§[-@sec-variables]); this is a property of the knot and the representation, not a general one (see the end of §[-@sec-universal]).

::: {#def-c1}
Expand the $c = 1$ part of the crosscap invariant in the fundamental representation as $$
g^{c=1} = \sum_\beta \lambda^\beta \sum_{g, J} N^{c=1}_{g,\beta,J}\, G^g q_r^{2J},\qquad 2J \in \mathbb{Z}.
$$ {#eq-Gexp} At $t = q$, $\sum_J N^{c=1}_{g,\beta,J}$ reduces to the $N^{c=1}_{g,\beta}$ of [@Marino09].
:::

For a knot whose unrefined $c = 2$ invariants vanish, such as a torus knot in the fundamental representation, the whole $c = 2$ part is its own refined part in the sense of §[-@sec-universal]; in general only the refined part $X_1^{c=2} = g^{c=2} - g^{c=2}|_{t=q}(\lambda \to \tilde\lambda)$ can be expected to carry the universal factor.

::: {#def-signprop}
## sign property

We say that a knot $K$ has the *sign property* in the fundamental representation if the following two conditions hold. Condition ($c{=}1$): the $c = 1$ part is $\sigma$-symmetric, and in its $G$-expansion ([-@eq-Gexp]) each $\lambda^\beta$ block has a common sign, equal to $\varepsilon_\beta$ when the block does not vanish at $t = q$, or is $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)\times$ a block with a common sign. Condition ($c{=}2$): the refined part of the $c = 2$ part is $(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)\times$ a polynomial whose coefficients have a common sign in each $\boldsymbol{a}$ block.
:::

::: {#cnj-criterion}
Every two-strand torus knot $T(2,2m+1)$ has the sign property in the fundamental representation; its $c = 2$ part is $-(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)\times$ a positive polynomial ([-@eq-Pim]).
:::

The evidence is Result [-@exr-torus] ($m \le 5$); items (N) and (P) of Result [-@exr-torus] are checks of the normalization, and the content on positivity is in ($c{=}1$) and ($c{=}2$). The factor $(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)$ vanishes at the $\mathrm{SO}(2)$ point, where knot invariants of an abelian group become trivial; $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)$ follows from vanishing at $t = q$ together with the parity (P). The sign property is not a property of all knots: it fails for $T(3,4)$ (§[-@sec-t34]) and for the algebraic cables of §[-@sec-cable]. Whether the Kauffman superpolynomials of [@GW05] for two-strand torus knots, which are positive, are related to our $c = 1$ part is not examined here *(open)*; we note that the refined $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ invariant $\mathcal{R}_{\ydA}$ itself is not positive in bold variables (§[-@sec-positivity]), so it is not a Poincaré polynomial of a Kauffman homology in these variables.

## Failure of ($c{=}1$) for $T(3,4)$ {#sec-t34}

::: {#exr-t34sign}
For the three-strand torus knot $T(3,4)$ in the fundamental representation ($\delta = 3$, $F = 12$; the general-$N$ invariant is obtained from the $D_N$ DAHA as in §[-@sec-generalN]), $g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA}$ is an integer Laurent polynomial, its $c = 1$ part is symmetric under $q \leftrightarrow 1/q$ at $t = q$, and the refined part of the whole $g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA}$ is divisible by the universal factor with all four $\boldsymbol{a}$ blocks of the quotient aligned. However, the $c = 1$ part is not $\sigma$-symmetric: the blocks $\lambda^{-10}$ and $\lambda^{-8}$ are asymmetric and only $\lambda^{-6}$ is symmetric, so ($c{=}1$) fails. The $c = 2$ part vanishes at $t = q$, is divisible by $(\boldsymbol{a}^2-\boldsymbol{q}^2)(\boldsymbol{t}^2-1)$, and the quotient has a common sign in each $\boldsymbol{a}$ block ($\boldsymbol{a}^{-11}$ and $\boldsymbol{a}^{-9}$ with opposite signs), so ($c{=}2$) holds. Splitting the $\sigma$-asymmetric part of the $c = 1$ part by Lefschetz weight (§[-@sec-sigmaorigin]), each block has a common sign in all rows, alternating with $\beta$; the same pattern occurs for the cables (Result [-@exr-cable-largeN]).
:::

Thus the $\sigma$-symmetry of the $c = 1$ part, hence the $G$-expansion, is specific to two-strand torus knots among the knots examined; what holds for $T(3,4)$ is integrality, the universal factor and ($c{=}2$). Why the $c = 1$ part is $\sigma$-symmetric only for two-strand torus knots is not understood *(open)*.

# Integrality and the universal factor for higher representations at general $N$ {#sec-generalN}

## DAHA-Jones polynomials {#sec-daha}

The multi-box values of refined $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ theory cannot be obtained at general $N$ from the $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ computation of [@AgSc12]. We therefore compute the DAHA-Jones polynomials of [@Cherednik11], $$
JD_{r,s}(b) = \{\hat\gamma_{r,s}(P_b)\}/P_b(q^{-\rho_k}),
$$ {#eq-JD} directly on the polynomial representations of the $D_N$ and $\mathrm{GL}_N$ DAHA at generic $t$. Here $P_b$ is the Macdonald polynomial of the weight $b$, $\hat\gamma_{r,s}$ the lift to the DAHA of an element of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ with first column $(r,s)$, and $\{H\} := (H\cdot 1)(q^{-\rho_k})$ the evaluation of the image of $1$ under $H$ at the point $X = q^{-\rho_k}$, $\rho_k$ being the deformed half-sum of positive roots. We write $Z_{r,s}(b) := \{\hat\gamma_{r,s}(P_b)\}$ for the unnormalized value, so that $JD = Z/P_b(q^{-\rho_k})$. The conventions, the checks of the implementation and the interpolation in $N$ are described in Appendix [A](#sec-app-code); the composites $(\alpha;\bar\beta)$ of the cover are computed on the $\mathrm{GL}_N$ side, extending the DAHA computations of composite invariants of [@CE15] to general $N$ (by interpolation), to the uniform normalization, and to $|\alpha| = 3$.

For a torus knot $T(2,n)$, $n = 2m+1$, set $F := rs = 2n$ and write the framing eigenvalue of a weight $b$ as $T_b = q^{(b,b)/2}t^{(b,\rho)}$. The unnormalized $D_N$ value $Z$ equals $T_R^{-F}$ times the mirror of the fixed-$N$ invariant $W_R$ in the uniform normalization; on the $\mathrm{GL}_N$ side $$
W_b = \mathop{\mathrm{mirror}}\bigl(Z_b/M_b\bigr),\qquad M_b := T_b^{-F}\, t^{\mathsf{c}_K\,|b|(N-1)},
$$ {#eq-Mb} with a knot-dependent constant $\mathsf{c}_K$ ($\mathsf{c}_K= m+1$ for $T(2,2m+1)$; for the cables see Result [-@exr-cable-interp]). The factor $t^{\mathsf{c}_K|b|(N-1)}$ was read off from the data of $(1), (2), (1,1)$ and predicted correctly for the other representations (Result [-@exr-daha]); we have no derivation of it from the $\mathrm{U}(1)$ part of $\mathrm{GL}_N$. The reduced invariant $\mathcal{R}_R(N) = T_R^{-F}\,\mathop{\mathrm{mirror}}(Z(N))/K_R(t^\rho)$ is interpolated as a Laurent polynomial in $t^N$ and checked at values of $N$ not used in the interpolation (Appendix [A.2](#sec-app-interp), Table [-@tbl-interp]). This gives the refined $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ invariants at general $N$ for the trefoil with two to four boxes, and for $T(2,5)$, $T(2,7)$, $T(2,9)$ with two and three boxes.

## Crosscap part at large $N$

On the $\mathrm{SO}$ side with three boxes the kernel is converted to the $K$ basis with the inverse of the matrix of $D_N$ Koornwinder polynomials $K_R$ ($|R| \le 3$, $t^N$ formal). The cover is assembled from ordinary representations, the adjoint and composites.

::: {#exr-largeN}
The crosscap parts at general $N$ have the following properties.

With two boxes (trefoil, $T(2,5)$, $T(2,7)$, $T(2,9)$, and $\mathcal{C}_{13}$ in §[-@sec-cable]), the denominators of $g_{\ydB}, g_{\ydAA}$ are $2\times$ monomial $\times(1+t)$ and all $N$-dependent poles cancel. The combinations $g_{\ydB} + g_{\ydAA}$ and $(1+t)(g_{\ydB} - g_{\ydAA})$ are integer Laurent polynomials. The $(1+t)$ sits in the $p_2$ direction only, in agreement with $E_{\ydB} = -E_{\ydAA}$ of Remark [-@rem-Esector]. The hatted $\hat g_{\ydB}$, $\hat g_{\ydAA}$ keep the denominator $2(1+t)\times$ monomial, while $\hat g_{\ydB} + \hat g_{\ydAA}$ is an integer Laurent polynomial.

With three boxes (trefoil, $T(2,5)$, $T(2,7)$, $T(2,9)$), $g_{\ydC}, g_{\ydBA}, g_{\ydAAA}$ are integer Laurent polynomials without $(1+t)$ poles, as predicted by Proposition [-@prp-alld] (no $E$ in odd sectors). The hatted $\hat g_R$ is also an integer Laurent polynomial for generic $U$ (with three boxes the all-$d$ $g$ equals the odd-$d$ $g^{\mathrm{odd}}$ of [@Marino09]).

With four boxes (trefoil), all $N$-dependent poles cancel; the $(1+t)$ poles sit only in the power-sum directions $p_4$ and $p_2^2$ (all parts even), as predicted by Proposition [-@prp-alld]. The Schur components $g_R$, $|R| = 4$, have denominators $2\times$ monomial $\times(1+t)$ and $2(1+t)g_R$ is an integer Laurent polynomial. In the power-sum basis, with $g_\rho := \sum_R \chi_R(\rho)\,g_R$, the components $g_{(3,1)}$, $g_{(2,1,1)}$, $g_{(1^4)}$ are integer Laurent polynomials and $(1+t)g_{(4)}$, $(1+t)g_{(2,2)}$ are integer Laurent polynomials without the factor $2$. Accordingly the Schur combinations in which the two $E$ directions cancel, such as $g_{(4)} + g_{(3,1)}$, $g_{(2,1,1)} + g_{(1^4)}$ and $g_{(4)} - g_{(2,2)} - g_{(2,1,1)}$, are integer Laurent polynomials, as $g_{\ydB} + g_{\ydAA}$ is for two boxes. As a power series in $t$ the individual $g_R$ are not integral; integrality as a series holds for $f$ and $f^{\mathrm{cov}}$ separately, not for their difference with the factor $\tfrac12$. The components of degree $\le 3$ agree with the three-box values.

The two- and three-box values agree with the fixed-$N$ values at $t^N = t^2, t^3$ coefficient by coefficient. For four boxes the cover $f^{\mathrm{cov}}$ was checked independently: decomposing $P_\alpha(x)P_\beta(x^{-1})$ irreducibly as polynomials in $\mathrm{U}(5)$ ($t^N = t^3$) and evaluating each component with the uniformly normalized $\mathrm{U}(5)$ values (mostly constructed as in [@KN17]; the seven shapes not available there were computed with the $\mathrm{GL}_5$ DAHA) reproduces the large-$N$ $f^{\mathrm{cov}}$ to degree four. This checks the Pieri coefficients, the interpolation and the assembly independently of the DAHA. Finally, the hatted invariants of the $q$-side and the $t$-side of [@KN17] agree for the two-box $\mathrm{SO}$, cover and crosscap parts.
:::

::: {#exr-fixedN}
## fixed $N$

At fixed $N = 2, 3$, where the $\mathrm{SO}$ data are obtained from A-type data through $\mathrm{SO}(4) = \mathrm{SU}(2)^2$ and $\mathrm{SO}(6) = \mathrm{SU}(4)$, the hatted crosscap invariants of $T(2,2m+1)$, $m \le 3$, with $|R| \le 3$ are integer Laurent polynomials in all power-sum directions. The same holds at $N = 2$ for seven double-twist knots with $|R| \le 3$ (using the rectangular formulas of [@KNTZ19]), together with the uniform normalization of Result [-@exr-uniform]. At fixed $N$ the universal factor and the sign property cannot be tested, since $\lambda$ is not a free variable.
:::

## Dictionary with the unrefined theory at $t = q$

::: {#exr-marino}
At $t = q$ the $\mathrm{SO}$ invariants $W_R$ and the cover invariants $W_S$ agree exactly with the mirror images ($\lambda \to 1/\lambda$, $t_M \to 1/t_M$) of $G_R, H_S$ of [@Marino09] (standard framing), for $R, S \in \{(1), (2), (1,1)\}$. For the crosscap part, $g_{\ydA} = -\mathop{\mathrm{mirror}}(g^{\mathrm{Mar}}_{\ydA})$. With two boxes, $-\mathop{\mathrm{mirror}}(\hat g^{\mathrm{Mar}}_R)$ is obtained by converting the all-$d$ $g$ to odd $d$ by ([-@eq-odd]), subtracting the unknot values $\mp\tfrac12$, and hatting with $M(q^{-1})^{-1}$. Our value of $\hat g_{\ydB}$ for the trefoil differs from (4.8) of [@Marino09] in the $z^9$ term only; our computation gives $z^9(11\lambda^{12} - 78\lambda^{10} + 78\lambda^8 - 11\lambda^6)$, and the integrality of the BPS expansion is consistent with this value, so the printed coefficient appears to be a misprint (Appendix [D.5](#sec-app-unref)).
:::

The coefficient of $z^9$ in $\hat g_{\ydB}$ printed in the equation (4.8) just mentioned is, in our variable, $-11\lambda^{11} + 78\lambda^9 - 79\lambda^7 + 12\lambda^5$; it repeats the coefficient of $z^8$ and has odd powers of $\lambda$, whereas every other odd power of $z$ in (4.8) comes with even powers of $\lambda$. The overall sign $-1$ is a consequence of the dual Cauchy (fermionic) kernel. The exchange $R \leftrightarrow R^T$ appears at the level of $g^{\mathrm{odd}}$ ($g^{\mathrm{odd}}_{\ydB}$ corresponds to the mirror of $g^{\mathrm{Mar}}_{\ydAA}$) and cancels in the hatted invariants because the mirror maps $M(q^{-1}) \leftrightarrow M(q)$.

## Universal factor {#sec-universal}

For a (hatted) crosscap invariant $\hat g$ define its *refined part* $$
X_1 = \hat g - \hat g\big|_{t=q}(\lambda \to \tilde\lambda),\qquad \tilde\lambda= \lambda q_r.
$$ {#eq-X1}

::: {#exr-universal}
At the $\mathrm{SO}(2)$ point $\lambda^2 = t$ the invariant $\hat g$ is independent of $t$, i.e., $\hat g|_{\lambda^2 = t}$ equals $\hat g|_{t=q}$ at $\lambda^2 = q$. Equivalently, $X_1$ is divisible by $(q - t)(\lambda^2 - t)$ (divisibility by $(q - t)$ is automatic). This holds for the fundamental representation of $T(2,2m+1)$, $m \le 5$, for the two-box $\hat g_{\ydB}, \hat g_{\ydAA}$ and their sum for $T(2,3)$, $T(2,5)$, $T(2,7)$, $T(2,9)$, for the three-box $\hat g_R$ of the trefoil, $T(2,5)$, $T(2,7)$, $T(2,9)$, and for $(1+t)\hat g_R$ of the four-box trefoil. In bold variables $(q - t)(\lambda^2 - t) = \boldsymbol{q}^2\,(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)$, the same factor as in the $c = 2$ part of the fundamental representation and in $\hat C_{R,S}$ of the Hopf link.
:::

Since $\hat g|_{t=q}$ depends on $\lambda$, the shift in ([-@eq-X1]) is forced: among $X_k = \hat g - \hat g|_{t=q}(\lambda \to \lambda q_r^k)$, $-3 \le k \le 3$, only $k = +1$ is divisible by $(\lambda^2 - t)$ (checked for the fundamental representation and two boxes of $T(2,3)$, $T(2,5)$ and three boxes of the trefoil). At the $\mathrm{SO}(2)$ point the group is abelian and the unrefined invariant is trivial; whether the $t$-independence at this point can be derived (e.g., as a formal continuation to $N = 1$) has not been examined *(open)*.

::: {#cnj-structure}
Let $K$ be a knot and $R$ a Young diagram, and let $\hat g_R$ be its hatted refined crosscap invariant in the uniform normalization. If $|R|$ is odd, $\hat g_R$ is an integer Laurent polynomial and $$
\hat g_R = \hat g_R\big|_{t=q}(\lambda \to \tilde\lambda) + (\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)\cdot(\text{integer Laurent polynomial}).
$$ {#eq-structure} If $|R|$ is even, the same holds with $\hat g_R$ replaced by $2(1+t)\hat g_R$ on both sides: $2(1+t)\hat g_R$ is an integer Laurent polynomial and $$
2(1+t)\,\hat g_R = \bigl[2(1+q)\,\hat g_R\big|_{t=q}\bigr](\lambda \to \tilde\lambda) + (\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)\cdot(\text{integer Laurent polynomial}).
$$ {#eq-structure-even} The factor $(1+q)$ on the right cancels the pole of $\hat g_R|_{t=q}$ at $q = -1$ that comes from the $p_2$-type entries of $M(q^{-1})^{-1}$. For the two-box trefoil the quotient in ([-@eq-structure-even]) was computed in this form; ([-@eq-structure-even]) is equivalent to the divisibility of $X_1$ in Result [-@exr-universal] whenever $\hat g_R|_{t=q}$ vanishes at $\lambda^2 = q$, which holds for the two-box trefoil.
:::

The evidence is Result [-@exr-universal] (up to four boxes for the trefoil, three boxes for $T(2,5)$, $T(2,7)$, $T(2,9)$) and Result [-@exr-cable-largeN] for the cables.

We close this section with the status of the integrality conjecture of [@Marino09] after refinement. That conjecture has two layers: the hatted crosscap invariants are Laurent polynomials with integer coefficients, and their expansion in $z$ defines integers $\hat N_{R,g,c,\beta}$ labeled by the genus $g$ and the crosscap number $c$. After refinement the two layers behave differently.

The first layer survives in the form of Conjecture [-@cnj-structure]: $\hat g_R$ for $|R|$ odd and $2(1+t)\hat g_R$ for $|R|$ even are Laurent polynomials with integer coefficients, in the range of Result [-@exr-largeN]. The factor $2(1+t)$ is due to the all-$d$ definition and not to the refinement: at $t = q$ the all-$d$ $\hat g_R$ with $|R|$ even still has a pole at $q = -1$, which the odd-$d$ definition of [@Marino09] absorbs through ([-@eq-odd]). In terms of ([-@eq-alld]) the integers of [@Marino09] correspond to the frozen states $C$ and the term with $2(1+t)$ to the invariant states $E$ (Hypothesis [-@exm-E2]).

The second layer, integers labeled by the genus and by $c$, does not survive in general. The refined expansion in genus is the $G$-expansion, which exists only for $\sigma$-symmetric polynomials (§[-@sec-variables]). It is available for the fundamental representation of $T(2,2m+1)$, $m \le 5$, where it gives the integers $N^{c=1}_{g,\beta,J}$ of Definition [-@def-c1] and the factorized $c = 2$ part (Result [-@exr-torus]). It is not available for $T(3,4)$ (§[-@sec-t34]), for the cables (§[-@sec-cable]), or for two and three boxes (Result [-@exr-noG]), where the $c = 1$ part is not $\sigma$-symmetric; splitting it into $\sigma$-even and $\sigma$-odd parts gives $G$-expansions with half-integer coefficients (Result [-@exr-multibox-sigma]). For even numbers of boxes there is in addition the fact that the separation of $E$ and $C$ is not determined by the index (Proposition [-@prp-EC]), so the part to be expanded as a count of frozen states is itself not fixed. The two-box sum and the three-box directions do not contain $E$, so the failure of the $G$-expansion is independent of this ambiguity. A refined analog of $\hat N_{R,g,c,\beta}$ for higher representations is thus not available *(open)*; what we have there is the first layer, in the range of Result [-@exr-largeN], together with the universal factor.

# Algebraic cables of the trefoil {#sec-cable}

Beyond torus knots, refined $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ invariants have had no definition, since the $S$ and $T$ matrices of refined Chern--Simons theory only produce torus knots. For iterated torus knots, the iterated DAHA-Jones polynomial of [@CD14] is defined for any reduced root system and weight $b$ by $$
JD_{\vec r,\vec s}(b) = \bigl\{\hat\gamma_1\bigl(\cdots\hat\gamma_{\ell-1}\bigl((\hat\gamma_\ell(P_b)/P_b(q^{-\rho_k}))\!\Downarrow\bigr)\!\Downarrow\cdots\bigr)\bigr\}_{\mathrm{ev}},\qquad H\!\Downarrow\, := H\cdot 1,
$$ {#eq-iterJD} where $\gamma_\ell$ is the innermost pattern, $\gamma_1$ the companion, $\gamma_i$ lifts an element of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ with first column $(r_i, s_i)$, and $\{\cdot\}_{\mathrm{ev}}$ is the evaluation at $q^{-\rho_k}$; by Theorem 2.4 of [@CD14] the result does not depend on the choice of lifts. We adopt its $D_N$ value as the definition of the refined $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ invariant of an algebraic cable.

::: {#exm-cablecover}
The cover of an algebraic cable is given by the $\mathrm{GL}_N$ iterated DAHA-Jones polynomials in ordinary and composite representations, normalized by ([-@eq-Mb]) (Hypothesis [-@exm-cover] for cables).
:::

The examples are the $(2, \mathsf{q})$-cables of the trefoil, $\mathcal{C}_{13}$ ($\mathsf{q} = 13$) and $\mathcal{C}_{15}$ ($\mathsf{q} = 15$), with $\mathsf{q}$ measured in the Seifert framing of the companion. The pattern word has first column $(2, \mathsf{q} - 12)$, i.e., $\tau_+\tau_-$ for $(2,1)$ and $\tau_-\tau_+\tau_-$ for $(2,3)$ in the notation of Appendix [A.1](#sec-app-daha-conv), and the companion is the trefoil $\tau_+\tau_-^2$ (the cable is algebraic if and only if $\mathsf{q} > 12$). Non-algebraic cables are not treated. In the companion step the polynomial $f_1 = \hat\gamma_{\mathrm{pat}}(P_b)\cdot 1$ from the pattern step is applied as $f_1(\hat\gamma_{\mathrm{comp}}(X))\cdot 1$. For $D_N$, $f_1$ is invariant under the Weyl group of $D_N$ and, for the degrees relevant here ($\deg f_1 \le 2|b| < N$), also under that of $B_N$; it is expanded in a basis $H_\nu$ of $B_N$-symmetric Laurent polynomials indexed by partitions $\nu$ with $|\nu| \le \deg f_1$, so that $JD$ becomes a linear combination of the basis values $\{\hat\gamma_{\mathrm{comp}}(H_\nu)\}$, computed once per $N$ and shared between the two cables (the companion is common). The adjoint of the cover is expanded likewise in $H_\mu(X)H_\nu(X^{-1})$.

::: {#exr-cable-interp}
## normalization and general $N$ for cables

For the cables $\mathcal{C}_{13}$ and $\mathcal{C}_{15}$ the normalization is fixed as follows. The $\mathrm{GL}_N$ values agree up to a monomial with A-type values of the same cables computed with an independent implementation ($\mathrm{U}(2)$, $\mathrm{U}(3)$, $|b| \le 2$). The $D_N$ values differ from the mirror of the fixed-$N$ $W_R$ in the uniform normalization, built through $\mathrm{SO}(4) = \mathrm{SU}(2)^2$ and $\mathrm{SO}(6) = \mathrm{SU}(4)$, only by $T_R^{-F}$ with $F = \mathsf{p}\mathsf{q}$ ($26$ for $\mathcal{C}_{13}$, $30$ for $\mathcal{C}_{15}$), for $N = 2, 3$ in the fundamental representation. This is the torus-knot rule with $F = rs$ replaced by $\mathsf{p}\mathsf{q}$. The genus $\delta$ of ([-@eq-uniform]) is $8$ ($\mathcal{C}_{13}$) and $9$ ($\mathcal{C}_{15}$), from the genus formula $\delta \mapsto \mathsf{p}\delta + (\mathsf{p}-1)(\mathsf{q}-1)/2$ of a $(\mathsf{p},\mathsf{q})$-cable. On the $\mathrm{GL}_N$ side, ([-@eq-Mb]) with $F = \mathsf{p}\mathsf{q}$ and $\mathsf{c}_K= 10$ ($\mathcal{C}_{13}$), $12$ ($\mathcal{C}_{15}$) holds for six ordinary representations at $N = 2$--4; the constants $\mathsf{c}_K$ are empirical. Since the adjoint has $|b| = 0$, this fixes its normalization to $T_{\mathrm{adj}}^{-F}$.

The interpolation in $N$ (Appendix [A.2](#sec-app-interp), Table [-@tbl-cableinterp]) reproduces the values at the $N$ not used coefficient by coefficient. For $(1,1)$ of $\mathcal{C}_{13}$ the cancellations at small $N$ are strong, and the data for $N \le 14$ are needed to determine all coefficients (with $N \le 13$ three degrees in $q^{1/2}$ remain undetermined). The solution was then checked at $N = 2, 3$, where the cancellations are strongest, and at $N = 15$, which was not used in the interpolation; all coefficients agree in each case. The $(1,1)$ of $\mathcal{C}_{15}$ requires $N \ge 13$ and the largest basis element $(1,1,1,1)$, which exceeds the memory available to us, so the two-box crosscap part was computed for $\mathcal{C}_{13}$ only (the $(2)$ and the adjoint of $\mathcal{C}_{15}$ were interpolated, Table [-@tbl-cableinterp], but are not used).
:::

::: {#exr-cable-largeN}
## crosscap part of cables at large $N$

The crosscap parts of the cables have the following properties.

In the fundamental representation ($\mathcal{C}_{13}$, $\mathcal{C}_{15}$), $g_{\ydA}$ is an integer Laurent polynomial and its refined part is divisible by the universal factor $(q-t)(\lambda^2-t)$, with 6 of 9 ($\mathcal{C}_{13}$) and 8 of 11 ($\mathcal{C}_{15}$) $\boldsymbol{a}$ blocks of the quotient aligned. At $t = q$ the $c = 1$ part is symmetric under $q \leftrightarrow 1/q$, and the $c = 2$ part does not vanish (the unrefined $c = 2$ invariants of a cable are non-zero). With two boxes ($\mathcal{C}_{13}$) the structure is that of the two-box case of Result [-@exr-largeN], and the refined parts of $\hat g_{\ydA}, \hat g_{\ydB}, \hat g_{\ydAA}$ and of their sum are all divisible by the universal factor. The quotient for the two-box sum has 30 of 50 $\boldsymbol{a}$ blocks aligned (Table [-@tbl-signs]).

The sign property (Definition [-@def-signprop]) fails. As for ($c{=}1$), the $c = 1$ part is not $\sigma$-symmetric; only the extreme blocks ($\lambda^{-26}, \lambda^{-16}$ for $\mathcal{C}_{13}$; $\lambda^{-30}, \lambda^{-28}, \lambda^{-18}$ for $\mathcal{C}_{15}$) are symmetric, with aligned signs in their $G$-expansions. Splitting the $\sigma$-asymmetric part by Lefschetz weight (§[-@sec-sigmaorigin]), each block has a common sign in all rows, alternating with $\beta$, as for $T(3,4)$. As for ($c{=}2$), the refined part of the $c = 2$ part is divisible by the universal factor, but the quotient has mixed signs within the $\boldsymbol{a}$ blocks (3 of 4 blocks mixed for $\mathcal{C}_{13}$, 3 of 5 for $\mathcal{C}_{15}$); the whole $c = 2$ part is not divisible by $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)$, as it must not be since its unrefined limit is non-zero. The refined part of the $c = 1$ part, by contrast, has aligned signs in every $\boldsymbol{a}$ block (5 blocks for $\mathcal{C}_{13}$, 6 for $\mathcal{C}_{15}$); the counts 6/9 and 8/11 given above for the fundamental representation are the sums over the two parts.
:::

Thus for the cables what holds is integrality and the universal factor (Conjecture [-@cnj-structure]), while the sign property fails in both of its parts, in contrast to $T(3,4)$ where only ($c{=}1$) fails (§[-@sec-t34]). Whether the half-degree relation of §[-@sec-sigmaorigin] between the $c = 1$ part and the brane--image sector is modified for these knots has not been examined *(open)*. The normalization of the cover for the cables rests on Hypothesis [-@exm-cablecover] and on the empirical constants $\mathsf{c}_K$; the integrality and the universal factor at general $N$, which were not used in fixing them, are the checks of this choice.

# Refined $\mathrm{Sp}(2N)$ and the $\mathrm{SO}(-N)$ correspondence {#sec-sp}

The refined Chern--Simons theory of [@AM22] is defined for any root system by taking $k_\alpha = y$ uniformly and $q_\alpha = q^{(\alpha,\alpha)/2}$; for $C_N$ the parameter of the long roots becomes $u = t_{\mathrm{lng}} = t^2$.
