We implemented the $C_N$ DAHA of [@Cherednik11] ($t = t_{\mathrm{sht}}$, $u = t_{\mathrm{lng}}$) on the polynomial representation (checks in Appendix [A](#sec-app-code)). In this section the conventions are those of the DAHA side, in which $g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA} = W_{\mathrm{SO}} - W^{\mathrm{cov}}_{\ydA}$ with $W^{\mathrm{cov}}_{\ydA}$ the mirror image of $\tfrac12 h_{\ydA}$ of ([-@eq-hg]) in the uniform normalization; the relation to the sign conventions of §[-@sec-torus] is the mirror of the relation for the crosscap part in Result [-@exr-marino].

::: {#exm-spcover}
The cover of the refined $\mathrm{Sp}(2N)$ theory is the same function of $\lambda$ as for $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$, with $\lambda = t^{N+1/2}$ ($a = \lambda^2 = t^{2N+1}$).
:::

::: {#exr-cn}
For the $C_N$ DAHA and the refined $\mathrm{Sp}(2N)$ invariants the following hold. At $u = 1$ the values agree exactly with the $D_N$ DAHA-Jones polynomials in the fundamental representation ($N = 2, 3$; $T(2,3)$, $T(2,5)$). They agree with $\mathcal{H}^C_{3,2}(\omega_1; q, t, u, a_{\mathrm{C}})$ of [@Cherednik11] at $a_{\mathrm{C}} = -t^{N-1}$ up to a monomial (rank $N = 2, 3, 4$). From the values at $N = 2, \dots, 8$ we reconstructed the hyper-polynomials $\mathcal{H}^C_{2m+1,2}(\omega_1)$ as polynomials in $a_{\mathrm{C}}$; to our knowledge the formula for $T(2,5)$ does not appear in [@Cherednik11] or [@CE15].

In the $\mathrm{SO}$ convention, with $W_{\mathrm{SO}} = \mathop{\mathrm{mirror}}[\mathcal{H}^C(u{=}1, a_{\mathrm{C}}{=}-\lambda/t^{1/2})]\cdot\dim_V^{\mathrm{SO}}(\lambda)\cdot(t^{1/2}/\lambda)^{2m}$ the difference $W_{\mathrm{SO}} - W^{\mathrm{cov}}_{\ydA}$ reproduces the $g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA}$ of Result [-@exr-torus], and the monomial $(t^{1/2}/\lambda)^{2m}$ is the only one for which it does. For $\mathrm{Sp}$, with $a_{\mathrm{C}} = -t^{N-1}$, $u = t^2$ and Hypothesis [-@exm-spcover], the monomial is fixed to the same $(t^{1/2}/\lambda)^{2m}$ as for $\mathrm{SO}$ by the cancellation of the pole at $t = 1$ and the Kauffman form at $t = q$, and for $T(2,3)$, $T(2,5)$ $$
g^{\mathrm{Sp}}_{\ydA}(\boldsymbol{a}, \boldsymbol{q}, \boldsymbol{t}) = -\,g^{\mathrm{SO}}_{\ydA}(-\boldsymbol{a}, \boldsymbol{q}, \boldsymbol{t})
$$ {#eq-sp1} holds coefficient by coefficient.
:::

Since $c = 1$ is assigned to even and $c = 2$ to odd powers of $\boldsymbol{a}$, ([-@eq-sp1]) says $C^{\mathrm{Sp}} = -C_{c=1} + C_{c=2}$: the rule of [@Marino09] that $\mathrm{SO}$ and $\mathrm{Sp}$ differ by the sign of the $c = 1$ terms survives refinement in these two examples. This independently supports the assignment of $c$, and is, to our knowledge, the first check that the refined $\mathrm{Sp}(2N)$ theory of [@AM22] is consistent for open strings.

The same structure holds with two boxes. The $C_N$ Macdonald polynomials $P_{2\varepsilon_1}$, $P_{\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2}$ were obtained from the triangular matrix of the Macdonald operator, and the values at $N = 2, \dots, 9$ were interpolated as rational functions of $t^N$ (at $u = 1$ they agree with the $D_N$ two-box values and with $\mathcal{H}^C_{3,2}(\omega_2)$ of [@Cherednik11] up to a monomial).

::: {#exr-sp2}
For the refined $\mathrm{Sp}(2N)$ trefoil with two boxes, $g^{\mathrm{Sp}}_{\ydB} + g^{\mathrm{Sp}}_{\ydAA}$ and $(1+t)(g^{\mathrm{Sp}}_{\ydB} - g^{\mathrm{Sp}}_{\ydAA})$ are integer Laurent polynomials, with the same all-$d$ structure as for $\mathrm{SO}$ (Proposition [-@prp-alld]), and $E^{\mathrm{Sp}}(t{=}-1) = E^{\mathrm{SO}}(t{=}-1)$ coefficient by coefficient. At the level of colored invariants $W_R^{\mathrm{Sp}}(\boldsymbol{a}) = (-1)^{|R|}\,W_R^{\mathrm{SO}}(-\boldsymbol{a})$ holds exactly. For the crosscap parts $$
\begin{aligned}
f^{\mathrm{Sp}}_{\ydB}(\boldsymbol{a}) - f^{\mathrm{SO}}_{\ydB}(-\boldsymbol{a}) &= \psi^2[\Delta], \qquad f^{\mathrm{Sp}}_{\ydAA}(\boldsymbol{a}) - f^{\mathrm{SO}}_{\ydAA}(-\boldsymbol{a}) = -\psi^2[\Delta], \\
\Delta &= 1 - \mathrm{even}_{\boldsymbol{a}}\big(g^{\mathrm{SO}}_{\ydA}\big) =\frac{(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)(\boldsymbol{a}^2\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)(\boldsymbol{a}^2\boldsymbol{q}^2\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)}{\boldsymbol{a}^6\boldsymbol{q}^2\boldsymbol{t}^4},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-sp2} the same for $g$, where $\psi^2$ is the Adams operation squaring $q, t, \boldsymbol{a}^2$ and $\mathrm{even}_{\boldsymbol{a}}$ denotes the part with even powers of $\boldsymbol{a}$ ($g^{\mathrm{SO}}_{\ydA}$ is the $g^{\mathrm{true}}_{\ydA}$ of ([-@eq-trefoil1]); in the sign convention of §[-@sec-setup], $\Delta = \mathrm{even}_{\boldsymbol{a}}(g_{\ydA}) + 1$ up to the factor of the uniform normalization). The hatted $p_1^2$ component $(g_{\ydB} + g_{\ydAA})/z_q$, denoted $X$ here, satisfies $X^{\mathrm{Sp}}(\boldsymbol{a}) = +X^{\mathrm{SO}}(-\boldsymbol{a})$, whereas for the fundamental representation the sign is $-$, cf. ([-@eq-sp1]).
:::

Relations ([-@eq-sp1]) and ([-@eq-sp2]), obtained for $T(2,3)$ and $T(2,5)$ in the fundamental representation and for the trefoil with two boxes, are refined versions of the classical correspondence $\mathrm{Sp}(N) = \mathrm{SO}(-N)$ with $R \to R^T$ [@Cvitanovic08; @MV10]. Whether they follow from a duality of the $C_N$ and $D_N$ DAHA at the level of Koornwinder polynomials has not been examined *(open)*. The two-box computation is restricted to the trefoil ($T(2,5)$ would need the values for all $N \le 13$ for the interpolation, beyond the current implementation).

::: {#rem-unlabeled-1}
*Remark 42*. In the power-sum components $Z_\rho$ of the generating function one finds $Z_1^{\mathrm{Sp}}(\boldsymbol{a}) = -Z_1^{\mathrm{SO}}(-\boldsymbol{a})$, $Z_{11}^{\mathrm{Sp}}(\boldsymbol{a}) = Z_{11}^{\mathrm{SO}}(-\boldsymbol{a})$, $Z_2^{\mathrm{Sp}}(\boldsymbol{a}) = Z_2^{\mathrm{SO}}(-\boldsymbol{a}) + 1$: the sign is $(-1)^{|\rho|}$ and only the $p_2$ direction is shifted by the constant $1$, which is the trace of the identity in the conversion to power sums and equals the $\boldsymbol{a}$-even part of the unknot crosscap in the fundamental representation ($+1$ for $\mathrm{SO}$, $-1$ for $\mathrm{Sp}$). In the difference $\psi^2[\Delta]$ of $f$, the piece $\psi^2[\mathrm{even}(g_{\ydA})]$ arises because the rule for the fundamental representation flips only the sign of the $\boldsymbol{a}$-even ($c = 1$) part, whereas the even part of the $d = 2$ Adams term $\tfrac12\psi^2[f_{\ydA}]$ does not follow this rule; the remaining $\psi^2[1]$ is the constant shift of $Z_2$. That $E$ does not change sign under the projection to $\mathrm{Sp}$ is consistent with the unrefined correspondence: using $E_{\ydB} = -E_{\ydAA}$, the sign flip and the transposition cancel. Since $\psi^2$ ($\lambda \to \lambda^2$) does not commute with $\boldsymbol{a}\to -\boldsymbol{a}$, there is no simple rule at the level of $f$ and $g$ in the $p_2$ direction.
:::

# Structure of the cover {#sec-cover}

## Setup {#sec-cover-setup}

The free energy $f^{\mathrm{cov}}$ of the cover $\mathrm{U}(N_A)$ is determined by A-type data alone, and the splitting of the cover described in this section is not needed to compute $g$. However, the source of $E$ (states invariant under $\tilde I$) lies in the brane--image sector of the cover, so the structure of the cover is needed to read off the structure of $g$. We split the cover into brane and image, find that the brane--brane sector is the invariant of [@KN17] itself, and identify the brane--image sector as a space of states. Further structure of the fixed sector (other torus knots, composites, the sector with two brane and two image boxes) is collected in Appendix [C](#sec-app-fixed).

Throughout this section $a = \lambda^2$, $q^{1/2}$ and $t^{1/2}$ are written as such, and $$
\kappa = \frac{(1 - a)(1 - q)}{(1 - t)(1 - qa/t)}
$$ {#eq-kappa} is the contraction term in the expansion of the adjoint, $\langle P_{\ydA}(x)P_{\ydA}(x^{-1})\rangle = W_{(1;\bar1)} + \kappa$. We write $V := 1 + t + qt$ and $\mathrm{Sym}^kV := h_k(1, t, qt)$ for the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial in the three weights $1, t, qt$; $V$ arises here as the Fock space of three cells generated by the contraction term $\kappa$ (Proposition [-@prp-rows]), and happens to have the three terms of the reduced superpolynomial of the trefoil in suitable variables. For $T(2,2m+1)$, $S$ denotes its reduced superpolynomial written in the same variables as $V$ (so $S = V$ for the trefoil), and $\psi^2$ is $(q, t) \to (q^2, t^2)$.

## Splitting into brane and image {#sec-split}

Writing the generating function of the cover with brane ($Y$) and image ($Y'$) probes, we find the following for the two-box trefoil and $T(2,5)$, and for the brane--image sector with boundary factors removed also for $T(2,7)$ (all blocks are listed in Appendix [D.4](#sec-app-cover); the three-box invariants have not been split).

The brane--brane sector is the $\mathrm{U}(N_A)$ invariant of [@KN17] itself: up to the factor $(t/q)^{\delta|R|/2}$ of the uniform normalization, $(t^{-1/2} - t^{1/2}) f^{\mathrm{bb}}_R$ agrees coefficient by coefficient with the $t$-side $f^{\bar t}_R$ of [@KN17] ($a = \lambda^2 = t^{N_A}$, mirror) for $R = (1), (2), (1,1)$, and the hatted version (the $p_1^2$ component divided by $z_q$, the $p_2$ component by $z_q^+$, i.e., $M(q^{-1})\otimes M(q^{-1})$ in the power-sum basis) agrees with $\hat f$ of [@KN17] with $R \leftrightarrow R^T$ because of the mirror (trefoil and $T(2,5)$). It therefore admits a $G$-expansion with aligned signs for all $\beta$, which is the positivity conjectured in [@KN17].

For the brane--image sector $\mathcal{B}= W_{(1;\bar1)} + \kappa - W_{\ydA}^2$, $(t^{-1/2} - t^{1/2})\mathcal{B}/z_q$ is an integer Laurent polynomial and $\sigma$-symmetric. Most $\lambda^\beta$ blocks are either aligned or $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)\times$ aligned; mixed blocks are $\lambda^{-8}$ for the trefoil and the four central blocks $\lambda^{-16}$--$\lambda^{-10}$ for $T(2,5)$. The brane--image sector of the oriented cover carries the same universal factor $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)$ as the crosscap. The division of $\mathcal{B}$ by $z_q$ is explained by Proposition [-@prp-rows]: $(1-t)\mathcal{B}= t(t - \lambda^2)(\lambda^2 - 1)(q - 1)(\lambda^2 q - 1)\,\mathcal{N}$, where $(q-1)$ is the $q$-side factor of the refined measure $(q-1)(t-1)$ of the annular string between brane and image and $(t-1)$ cancels against the tower $1/(1-t)$. The fixed-sector index of the unknot with framing $\mathsf f$, $(\lambda^2-1)(q-1)\sum_{k<\mathsf f}(\lambda^2q)^{\mathsf f-1-k}t^k$, carries the same factor. The boundary factors of brane and image are symmetric. The $\lambda$ boundary factor $(t-\lambda^2)(\lambda^2-1)(\lambda^2q-1)$ alternates in sign between $\lambda^\beta$ blocks, and most of the mixing of $\mathcal{B}/z_q$ is due to it. When $\mathcal{N}$ (with all boundary factors removed) is expanded in $G$ (Appendix [D.4](#sec-app-cover)), all blocks are aligned for the trefoil, and only the block $k = 2m$ ($\lambda^{-(6+4m)}$) is mixed for $T(2,5)$ and $T(2,7)$. We call it the *switching block*: it is the block where the universal series $\mathrm{Sym}^kV$ turns into the knot-dependent part (Conjecture [-@cnj-closedform]), $n_{2m} = \mathrm{Sym}^{2m}V - S\otimes S$, and $\mathrm{Sym}^{2m}V$ and $S\otimes S$ separately have aligned $G$-coefficients ($m \le 3$). The mixing of the brane--image sector is therefore the structure $-S\otimes S$ of the space of states itself, a subtraction of pairs of states, distinct both from the non-positivity inherent to the composite values $R_{\mathrm{adj}}$ (§[-@sec-composite], [@CE15]) and from the crosscap problem.

## The space of states of the lowest fixed sector {#sec-principle}

In the lowest fixed sector (brane 1, image 1, written $n = 1$ after the number of boundary pairs), $E$ can be constructed from an identification of the space of states. Split the support $\mathcal{N}$ by powers of $\lambda^{-2}$ into blocks $k = 0, \dots, K = 4m-1$ for $T(2,2m+1)$; the block $n_k$ is the coefficient of $\lambda^{-(6+2k)}$ in $\mathcal{N}$ normalized by $q^{-(2+k)}$. The blocks $k \le 2m$ are called the *lower series* and $k > 2m$ the *upper series* (Figure [-@fig-series]).

![The blocks $n_k$ of the fixed sector $\mathcal{N}$ of a two-strand torus knot $T(2,2m+1)$ (Conjecture [-@cnj-closedform]): the lower series is universal, the switching block $k = 2m$ subtracts the square of the reduced superpolynomial, and the upper series is the dual of the lower one with knot-dependent corrections. The switching block is the only one whose $G$-expansion has mixed signs.](fig3.svg){#fig-series}

::: {#cnj-closedform}
## closed form of the fixed sector

For $T(2,2m+1)$, with $K = 4m-1$, $$
\begin{gathered}
n_k = \mathrm{Sym}^kV\ (k<2m),\qquad n_{2m} = \mathrm{Sym}^{2m}V - S\otimes S,\\
n_{K-j} = -t^{K-2j}\bigl[\mathrm{Sym}^jV + (q-t)\,R_j\bigr]\ (0 \le j \le 2m-2),
\end{gathered}
$$ {#eq-nk} where for $j = m + j' \ge m$ the correction is $R_{m+j'} = t^{m-1-j'}F_{j'}$ with $F_{j'}$ independent of the knot, $$
\sum_{j'\ge 0}F_{j'}z^{j'} = \frac{1 + (2t + t^2 + qt + 2qt^2)z + qt^3z^2}{(1-z)(1-qtz)(1-t^2z)(1-q^2t^2z)}
$$ {#eq-Fgen} ($F_{j'}$ has $\binom{2j'+3}{3}$ states); the $R_j$ with $j < m$ are not covered by ([-@eq-Fgen]). The involution $\tilde I$ acts on $V$ as the involution $\mathrm{diag}(1,1,-1)$ (its dual on the upper series), on $S\otimes S$ as the exchange of factors (trace $\psi^2 S$), and on the correction as $(-1)^{m+j'+1}t^{m-1-j'}\psi^2(X_{j'})$ with $X_{j'} = \mathrm{Sym}^{j'}V + t\,\mathrm{Sym}^{j'-1}V$ (generating function $(1+tz)/((1-z)(1-tz)(1-qtz))$, $(j'+1)^2$ states), the remaining states of $F_{j'}$ being pairs: $F_{j'} = \psi^2 X_{j'} + 2P_{j'}$ with $\sum P_{j'}z^{j'} = tz(V' + qt^2z)/((1-z)(1-qtz)(1-t^2z)(1-q^2t^2z))$, $V' = 1 + q + qt$. $E$ is the corresponding trace of $\tilde I$.
:::

::: {#exr-principle}
Conjecture [-@cnj-closedform] was obtained as follows and holds in the following range. The blocks ([-@eq-nk]) agree with the computed $\mathcal{N}$ coefficient by coefficient for $T(2,3)$--$T(2,15)$, and ([-@eq-Fgen]) with $j' \le 5$. The action of $\tilde I$ was fitted on $T(2,3)$--$T(2,9)$: for $T(2,3)$ and $T(2,5)$ the resulting $E$ reproduces in every monomial the unique $E$ determined by (E1) and (E2) with Hypothesis [-@exm-QP] replaced by the sign rule of §[-@sec-EC], and for $T(2,9)$ the form of $X_{2}$ was selected uniquely among 32 variants by the rows and the support of (E1). For $T(2,11)$, $T(2,13)$, $T(2,15)$ the $E$ so constructed satisfies (E1) and (E2) as a prediction. Comparing monomial by monomial $\mathcal{N}= (1-t)\mathcal{B}/(t(t-\lambda^2)(\lambda^2-1)(q-1)(\lambda^2q-1))$ and $\tilde{\mathcal{N}} = E/(t(t-\lambda^2)(\lambda^2+1)(q+1)(\lambda^2q+1))$ with the boundary factors removed, $|\tilde e_\omega| \le |c_\omega|$ and $\tilde e_\omega \equiv c_\omega \pmod 2$ hold for all monomials $\omega$ of $T(2,3)$--$T(2,15)$; in the lower series $|\tilde e_\omega| = |c_\omega|$ (all states invariant under $\tilde I$), and pairs exchanged by $\tilde I$ first appear at $k \ge 2m$. Thus $E$ reads as a signed partial sum of numbers of states. A simpler sign rule ($(-1)^{\deg_q}$ on the lower series and $(-1)^{\deg_t}$ on the upper series) fixes $E$ for $T(2,3)$ and $T(2,5)$ but has no solution for $T(2,7)$; the plethystic logarithm of ([-@eq-Fgen]) has negative coefficients, so the upper series cannot be read as a Fock space of positive BPS generators (Appendix [C](#sec-app-fixed)).
:::

::: {#prp-rows}
Let $\xi = \lambda^{-2}$. Write the mirror of the fundamental representation of the cover, expanded in powers of $\lambda^{-2}$ (its "$a$-rows"), as $R_{\ydA} = q^{-\delta/2}t^{-\delta/2}\xi^\delta R(\xi)$ with $R(y) = \sum_j \rho_j y^j$, and the adjoint $(1;\bar1)$ as $R_{\mathrm{adj}} = q^{-2\delta}\xi^{2\delta}A(\xi)$ with $A(y) = \sum_j \alpha_j y^j$. Then the blocks of the fixed sector $\mathcal{N}$ of $n = 1$ satisfy $$
(q-1)(t-1)\sum_k \bigl(n_k - \mathrm{Sym}^kV\bigr) y^k = y^{2\delta-1}\Bigl[\frac{A(qy)}{1-ty} - \frac{R(qy)^2(1-qy)}{(1-y)(1-qty)}\Bigr].
$$ {#eq-rows} Consequently every block $n_k$ is a Laurent polynomial in $q, t$ if and only if $A - R^2$ is divisible by $(q-1)(t-1)$, i.e., $A = R^2 + (q-1)(t-1)\Gamma$ with $\Gamma$ a Laurent polynomial, and then $$
\sum_k n_k y^k = \frac{1 - y^{2\delta}R(qy)^2}{(1-y)(1-ty)(1-qty)} + \frac{y^{2\delta-1}\Gamma(qy)}{1-ty}.
$$ {#eq-rows2}
:::

::: {.proof}
By definition $\mathcal{N}= (1-t)\bigl[R_{\mathrm{adj}}(d_{\ydA}^2 - \kappa) + \kappa - (t/q)^\delta R_{\ydA}^2 P_{\ydA}^2\bigr]/D$ with $d_{\ydA}^2 = (\lambda - \lambda^{-1})^2/(t^{1/2} - t^{-1/2})^2$ the square of the quantum dimension of the fundamental representation, $P_{\ydA} = t^{1/2}\lambda^{-1}(1 - \lambda^2)/(1-t)$ its Macdonald dimension, $(t/q)^\delta$ the factor of the uniform normalization, and $D = t(t - \lambda^2)(\lambda^2 - 1)(q - 1)(\lambda^2 q - 1)$. Both $R_{\mathrm{adj}}$ and $(t/q)^\delta R_{\ydA}^2$ carry the prefactor $q^{-2\delta}\xi^{2\delta} = y^{2\delta}$ with $y = \xi/q$, so $\delta$ enters only through this power, and $\sum_k n_k y^k = q^2\xi^{-3}\mathcal{N}$ written in $y$ (the normalization of the blocks). The identity ([-@eq-rows]) is then a rational identity in $y, q, t$ and the coefficients $\rho_j, \alpha_j$, which is verified by direct computation (the $\kappa$ term gives $\sum_k \mathrm{Sym}^kV\,y^k = 1/((1-y)(1-ty)(1-qty))$). Since $(1-y)(1-qty) - (1-qy)(1-ty) = -y(q-1)(t-1)$, the bracket in ([-@eq-rows]) equals $(A(qy) - R(qy)^2)/(1-ty)$ plus a multiple of $(q-1)(t-1)$ with Laurent coefficients, which gives the second statement.
:::

::: {#exr-rows}
For the fourteen torus knots $T(2,3)$--$T(2,15)$, $T(3,4)$, $T(3,5)$, $T(3,7)$, $T(3,8)$, $T(3,10)$, $T(4,5)$, $T(4,7)$, writing $\Gamma(y) = \sum_j\gamma_j y^j$, one has $\gamma_0 = 0$ and $\gamma_1 = (2\rho_0\rho_1 - \rho_1^2)/q$, so the switching block is $n_{2\delta} = \mathrm{Sym}^{2\delta}V - (\rho_0 - \rho_1)^2$. The factor of the square is always the top two rows $\rho_0 - \rho_1$ of the fundamental representation; for two strands this is the reduced superpolynomial (two rows), and for $T(3,4)$ it is the reduced superpolynomial with its third row $t^3$ dropped. Since $\mathcal{N}$ is determined by the cover data of the adjoint and the fundamental representation alone, this factor and $K = rs - 3$ were predicted correctly for $T(3,5)$, $T(3,7)$, $T(3,8)$, $T(3,10)$, $T(4,5)$, $T(4,7)$. The deepest block is $n_K = -t^{K-p+2}h_{p-2}(q,t)$ for a torus knot with $p = 2, 3, 4$ strands, where $h_k(q,t)$ is the complete homogeneous polynomial in $q, t$.
:::

For $n = 1$ the separation of $E$ and $C$ (Proposition [-@prp-EC]) is thus resolved, conjecturally, by the identification of the space of states. The structure $S\otimes S$ at the switching block and the corrections $F_{j'}$ are specific to two-strand torus knots: for $T(3,4)$ the upper series has a different form (Appendix [C](#sec-app-fixed)). For $n = 2$ (two brane and two image boxes) $E$ is determined up to $\lambda^{-12}$ and undetermined from $\lambda^{-14}$ on (Appendix [C.3](#sec-app-n2)).

# Obstructions for multi-box crosscap invariants {#sec-positivity}

## Interpretation of signs and the sign statistics {#sec-signs}

BPS numbers are indices with $(-1)^F$, not numbers of states; the positivity conjectured in [@KN17] means that refinement undoes the cancellation of $(-1)^F$ and exposes the numbers of states resolved by spin. For the orientifold, $\tilde I$ breaks $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L\times\mathrm{SU}(2)_R$ to $\mathrm{U}(1)_1\times\mathrm{U}(1)_2$ [@AgSc12], so non-orientable states need not form complete spin multiplets, and in the interpretation of [@PU14] the number of frozen states is a difference $n^+ - n^-$ weighted by the orientifold parity. The positivity question for the crosscap part should therefore be posed as in §[-@sec-criterion]: in a suitable multiplet basis, the coefficients of each block align with the unrefined sign $\varepsilon_\beta$. Positivity is a question at the BPS level: the refined $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ Chern--Simons invariants themselves are not positive in bold variables even in the fundamental representation (4 of the 9 terms of $\mathcal{R}_{\ydA}$ of the trefoil are negative), and it is remarked in [@Cherednik11] that there is "almost no positivity" for hyper-polynomials of type $C$--$D$ even for the minimal weight.

::: {#exr-signs}
Writing the quotient $X_1/((\boldsymbol{t}^2-1)(\boldsymbol{a}^2-\boldsymbol{q}^2))$ of the refined part by the universal factor in bold variables, the numbers of $\boldsymbol{a}$ blocks with aligned signs are those of Table [-@tbl-signs]. Three alternatives do not align the signs either (negative results). A change of the basis on the right-hand side of the free energy (Hall--Littlewood, $P_R(Y; q, t)$, $P_R(Y; t, q)$, $Q_R$, modified Macdonald) does not help: for the two-box trefoil the $(1,1)$ component in the $P(Y;t,q)$ basis improves the count to 8/11 (the number of blocks depends on the basis), but for the Hopf link and for three boxes at fixed $N$ this basis is worse or breaks integrality. Passing to the second-quantized exponents, i.e., the exponents of the product form of $\tilde Z$ expanded in power series in $t$ (towers of modes), leaves a fraction of mixed blocks of about 13% for the two-box trefoil (16 of 123, 15 of 110), about 34% for the two-box $T(2,5)$, 38--44% for the three-box trefoil, 61--66%, 67--71%, 74--77% for the three-box $T(2,5)$, $T(2,7)$, $T(2,9)$, and about 42% for the two-box $\mathcal{C}_{13}$. Finally, a search for symmetries in $(q^{1/2}, q_r)$, i.e., for a change of multiplet variables, did not align the signs.
:::

  object                                                                                       aligned blocks / all blocks
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------
  fundamental, $T(2,2m+1)$ ($m \le 5$)                                                         all
  fundamental, $T(3,4)$                                                                        4/4
  fundamental, cables $\mathcal{C}_{13}$, $\mathcal{C}_{15}$                                   6/9, 8/11
  two-box sum $\hat g_{\ydB} + \hat g_{\ydAA}$: trefoil, $T(2,5)$, $T(2,7)$, $T(2,9)$   5/10, 6/18, 10/26, 14/34
  two-box sum, $\mathcal{C}_{13}$                                                              30/50
  three boxes $\hat g_{\ydC}, \hat g_{\ydBA}, \hat g_{\ydAAA}$: trefoil            2/15, 3/14, 2/13
  three boxes: $T(2,5)$                                                                        1/25, 1/24, 1/23
  three boxes: $T(2,7)$; $T(2,9)$                                                              1/35, 1/34, 1/33; 1/45, 1/44, 1/43
  four boxes $(1+t)\hat g_R$, trefoil, $R = (4), (3,1), (2,2), (2,1,1), (1^4)$                 1/22, 1/21, 2/21, 2/20, 0/18

  : Number of $\boldsymbol{a}$ blocks of the quotient $X_1/((\boldsymbol{t}^2-1)(\boldsymbol{a}^2-\boldsymbol{q}^2))$ with aligned signs over the total number of blocks. {#tbl-signs}

The fraction of aligned blocks decreases as the knot or the number of boxes grows. The aligned blocks concentrate at shallow powers of $\boldsymbol{a}$: the 30 aligned blocks of the two-box $\mathcal{C}_{13}$ are $\boldsymbol{a}^{-32}$--$\boldsymbol{a}^{-3}$, all negative, continuing the column $\boldsymbol{a}^{-8}$--$\boldsymbol{a}^{-3}$ aligned for the two-box $T(2,5)$, while the mixed blocks sit at $\boldsymbol{a}^{-52}$--$\boldsymbol{a}^{-33}$. By Proposition [-@prp-alld] and Corollary [-@cor-Efree], the two-box sum and the three-box directions do not depend on $E$, so the mixing is not caused by the $E$ ambiguity (the four-box Schur components contain $E$, so this argument does not cover the four-box rows). We attribute it to an inappropriate multiplet basis for the frozen states $C$ (a conjecture; we do not exclude that positivity itself fails).

## $\sigma$-asymmetry and the failure of the $G$-expansion {#sec-sigmaasym}

::: {#exr-noG}
The $c = 1$ part of the fundamental representation of $T(2,2m+1)$ is $\sigma$-symmetric, but for two and three boxes it is not, whether one takes $\hat g_R$, the sum, or the odd-$d$ version, and whether $c = 1$ is taken as the even powers of $\lambda$ or with the hatted parity rule of Result [-@exr-multibox-sigma]. The reduced $\mathrm{SO}$ invariants $\mathcal{R}_R$ have no symmetry with a monomial ratio under any combination of $\sigma$, $q\leftrightarrow t$, mirror, $\lambda \to \pm\lambda^{\pm1}q_\ell^{c_1}q_r^{c_2}$ ($|c_1|, |c_2| \le 2$) and $R \leftrightarrow R^T$.
:::

Since the $\mathrm{SO}$ side has no analog of the super-duality of type $A$, there is no reason for the $\mathrm{SO}$ $\hat f$ and $\hat g$ to be $\sigma$-symmetric (the $\hat f$ of the cover is $\sigma$-symmetric for each $R$). The asymmetry has two sources.

::: {#exr-multibox-sigma}
The $\sigma$-asymmetry of the multi-box $c = 1$ part decomposes into two parts.

The first is present already at $t = q$, where the $c$ of [@Marino09] is defined by the parity in $z = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}$ ($c = 1$ even in $z$, symmetric under $q \leftrightarrow 1/q$). The corresponding parity in $\lambda$ depends on the power-sum direction: it agrees with "$c = 1$ $\Leftrightarrow$ even powers of $\lambda$" in the directions without $p_2$ (fundamental, $p_1^2$, $p_3$, $p_1^3$) and is opposite in those with $p_2$ ($p_2$, $p_2 p_1$). For the hatted $\hat g_R = M(q^{-1})^{-1} g_R$ the $c = 1$ part is the part with $\beta \equiv |R| - 1 \pmod 2$ in $\lambda^\beta$ (even for the fundamental representation, odd for two boxes, even for three; the three-box $\hat g_R$ of the trefoil is an integer Laurent polynomial for generic $U$ and all three satisfy this). The $c = 2$ admixture in the even powers of $\lambda$ of the $p_2$ direction has the closed form $-2 z\,\Delta|_{t=q}\,(q^{4n}-1)/(q-1) \times$ monomial (containing $\lambda^4 q + \lambda^2(q^2+q+1) + q$ for $T(2,5)$), with $n = 2m+1$ and $\Delta$ as in ([-@eq-sp2]). This part of the asymmetry is present in the unrefined theory and disappears once the parity rule is applied.

The second is refined: even with the correct $c = 1$ the refined part is not $\sigma$-symmetric; prefactors, products of the fundamental representation, Adams corrections and transposition do not repair this. The $\sigma$-odd part is divisible by $\boldsymbol{q}^2(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)(q_\ell^2 - 1)$, i.e., up to a monomial by $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)(q_\ell- q_\ell^{-1})$, and vanishes at $t = q$: $\hat g^{c=1} = \Sigma_+ + (\boldsymbol{t}^2-1)(q_\ell- q_\ell^{-1})\,\Sigma_-$ with $\Sigma_\pm$ $\sigma$-symmetric and $G$-expandable. However $\Sigma_\pm$ are half-integral, and the $G$-expansion of $\Sigma_-$ is aligned in all blocks (alternating in $\beta$) for the trefoil but breaks for $T(2,5)$. For three boxes, splitting the $c = 1$ blocks by Lefschetz weight, the signs of the $\sigma$-asymmetric part are aligned in almost all blocks and alternate in $\beta$ for the trefoil, but for $T(2,5)$, $T(2,7)$ and $T(2,9)$ ($\hat g_{\ydC}, \hat g_{\ydBA}$) they align only in the lowest block and at most one more.
:::

The factor $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)$ is the universal factor of $c = 2$ (a twisted trace of $\mathrm{SU}(2)_r$), and $(q_\ell- q_\ell^{-1})$ is odd under the Weyl reflection of the Lefschetz $\mathrm{SU}(2)_\ell$. The multi-box $c = 1$ part contains states that are twisted by $\tilde I$ and have odd Lefschetz spin; the fundamental representation of two-strand torus knots has none. This may be the $G$-expansion counterpart of the statement in §[-@sec-EC] that $S_R$ does not act trivially in the fixed sector of a knot (a conjecture).

## Origin of the $\sigma$-symmetry {#sec-sigmaorigin}

In the variables $q_\ell= (qt)^{1/2}$, $q_r= (q/t)^{1/2}$ of [@KN17], $\sigma\colon q\mapsto t^{-1}, t\mapsto q^{-1}$ is $q_\ell\mapsto q_\ell^{-1}$ with $q_r$ fixed, the Weyl reflection of the Lefschetz $\mathrm{SU}(2)_\ell$ acting on the Jacobian. The $\sigma$-invariance of $\hat f$ in [@KN17] comes from the handle zero modes forming $\mathrm{SU}(2)_\ell$ doublets (each handle contributes $-(q_\ell+ q_\ell^{-1}) + (q_r+ q_r^{-1})$, which is $-G$ in our convention, §[-@sec-variables]), and the *Lefschetz weight* of a monomial is its power of $q_\ell$. Frozen states are M2-branes wrapped on the non-orientable surface $\hat\Sigma/I$, which carries no complex structure, so the Lefschetz $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ does not act on its $H^1$. There is therefore no reason to expect $\sigma$-symmetry of $C$, and this explains, conjecturally, why the $c = 1$ part of multi-box invariants has no $G$-expansion; the factors $T_\pm$ of $G = T_+T_-$ do not help (Appendix [B](#sec-app-closed)). That the $c = 1$ part in the fundamental representation *is* $\sigma$-symmetric for two-strand torus knots has a conjectural explanation as well. The $G$-degree of the $\lambda^\beta$ block of the $c = 1$ part is exactly half the $G$-degree of the $\lambda^{2\beta}$ block of the brane--image sector $(t^{-1/2}-t^{1/2})\mathcal{B}/z_q$ (for all $\beta$ of $T(2,3)$ and $T(2,5)$). The frozen states in the fundamental representation are quotients of brane--image annuli (Möbius strips); $g$ handles of the quotient correspond to $2g$ handles of the cover, and the handles of the quotient carry $G$. Whether this half-degree relation is modified for $T(3,4)$ and for the cables, where the $c = 1$ part is not $\sigma$-symmetric, has not been examined *(open)*.

## Separation of $E$ and $C$ {#sec-EC}

By Proposition [-@prp-EC] the separation of $E$ and $C$ needs information beyond the index. For the lowest fixed sector of two-strand torus knots it is provided by the identification of the space of states (§[-@sec-principle]). Attempts to determine $E$ for knots from the index together with conditions (E1), (E2) and various ansätze for the action of $\tilde I$ (partial sums of states, Adams-type forms, twisted traces with boundary factor $z_q$ or $z_q^+$, handle twists, sign rules) succeed for the Hopf link and the framed unknot but not for knots; they are reported in Appendix [C.2](#sec-app-attempts). For the unknot with framing $\mathsf f$ the result is unique:

::: {#exr-framed}
For the unknot with framing $\mathsf f$ the fixed-sector index is $\Phi(\mathsf f) = (\lambda^2-1)(q-1)\sum_{k<\mathsf f}(\lambda^2q)^{\mathsf f-1-k}t^k$. Imposing only (E1) and "$C$ integer Laurent at $t = q$" and enumerating all candidates, $E$ is unique for $\mathsf f = 1, 2, 3$: $$
E(\mathsf f) = (-1)^{\mathsf f}(\lambda^2+1)(q+1)\sum_{k<\mathsf f}(-1)^k(\lambda^2q)^{\mathsf f-1-k}t^k\times\text{monomial},
$$ {#eq-Eframed} i.e., $\tilde I$ acts on the $t$ tower by $(-1)^k$ ($e^{i\pi J_2}$).
:::

Here $J_2$ is the generator of rotations of the $z_2$ plane, on whose modes $t^l$ the involution acts by $(-1)^l$ (§[-@sec-index-setup]), and $S_R$ is the charge of the additional $\mathrm{U}(1)_R$ symmetry present for torus knots, in terms of which the refined index weighs a state by $t^{S_R - J_2}$. Since $\tilde I = I\otimes e^{i\pi J_2}$, the index sees only the combination $S_R - J_2$ of the spins. Determining $E$ for a knot therefore requires splitting the $t$-charge of the fixed-sector states into $J_2$ (sign under $\tilde I$) and $S_R$ (invariant), i.e., the numbers of states before cancellation corresponding to $\hat N_{\rho,g,\beta,J_r,S_R}$ of [@KN17]. For the unknot everything is $J_2$; for knots, states of equal charge carry different signs (computation, Appendix [C.2](#sec-app-attempts)). Under the assumption of [@KN17] that $S_R$ acts trivially on BPS states the sign would be fixed by the parity of the charge, so in the brane--image sector of a knot $S_R$ acts non-trivially (a conjecture). This is the quantum-number form of the ambiguity of Proposition [-@prp-EC].

Integrality gives a constraint on $E$, which is the refined form of the strong integrality condition recalled at the end of this paragraph. Integrality of $f = \tfrac12 f^{\mathrm{cov}} + \tfrac12 E/(1+t) + C$ in the all-$d$ form is equivalent to $E \equiv \Phi_{\mathrm{inv}} \pmod 2$ coefficient by coefficient, where $\Phi_{\mathrm{inv}}$ is the index of the invariant states ($\tfrac12[\Phi_{\mathrm{inv}}(1+t) + E(1-t)]/(1-t^2)$ is an integer series if and only if $\Phi_{\mathrm{inv}} + E \equiv 0 \pmod 2$). This is exactly the parity constraint of the integer programs of Appendix [A.4](#sec-app-ilp). The unrefined form of §4 of [@AgSc12] (agreement mod 2 of the oriented $f_{\ydA,\ydA}$ with the non-orientable $f_{\ydA}(q^2)$) is the shadow of this after $E$ and $C$ mix at $t = q$ through (E2).

## Non-positivity of the composite DAHA {#sec-composite}

The fixed-sector states come from the value $R_{\mathrm{adj}}$ of the adjoint $(1;\bar1)$ of the cover. If $R_{\mathrm{adj}}$ could be read as a Poincaré polynomial of a homology (positive coefficients), the numbers of states before cancellation would follow.

::: {#exr-adjpos}
## negative

The large-$N$ $R_{\mathrm{adj}}$ (the $\mathrm{GL}_N$ DAHA) has mixed signs even after the bold change of variables of [@KN17] applied with the mirror (7 of 19 terms negative for the trefoil, 25 of 56 for $T(2,5)$), and no monomial-parity sign rule (64 rules) aligns the coefficients.
:::

This agrees with the statement in the introduction of [@CE15] that composite DAHA superpolynomials have no positivity. A relation to annular HOMFLY-PT homology is not conjectured there either.

# Discussion and open problems {#sec-discussion}

We have defined a refined crosscap invariant for the $\mathrm{SO}(2N)$ refined Chern--Simons theory and examined its integrality, its structure and its signs. The following table lists the main statements with their status: derived, computed in a stated range, hypothetical or conjectural.

::: center
  statement                                                                                                                                                                                              grade                                                                                                                  where
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  $g$ is free of $N$-dependent poles; integer Laurent in odd sectors, $2(1+t)g$ integer in even sectors; agrees with [@Marino09] at $t = q$ for the fundamental representation and the two-box trefoil   computation                                                                                                            Results [-@exr-largeN], [-@exr-cable-largeN], [-@exr-marino]
  all-$d$ structure $g = \tfrac12 E/(1+t) + C$, $E$ only in fixed sectors, boundary factor $z_q^{n-1}(z_q^+)^n$                                                                                          derivation under Hypothesis [-@exm-classes]; agrees with computation   Propositions [-@prp-alld], [-@prp-boundary]; Result [-@exr-boundary]
  brane--brane sector $=$ refined LMOV invariants of [@KN17]                                                                                                                                             computation (trefoil, $T(2,5)$)                                                                                        §[-@sec-split]
  brane--image sector as a space of states                                                                                                                                                               computation for $T(2,3)$ to $T(2,15)$, with a conjectural closed form                                                  Conjecture [-@cnj-closedform], Result [-@exr-principle]
  cover given by A-type invariants; uniform normalization is framing zero; classification of states; frozen states match the odd-$d$ invariants at $t = q$; cover of cables and of $\mathrm{Sp}$         hypotheses                                                                                                             [-@exm-cover], [-@exm-framing], [-@exm-classes], [-@exm-E2], [-@exm-cablecover], [-@exm-spcover]
  sign property for $T(2,2m+1)$; closed form of $\Pi_m$; universal-factor structure                                                                                                                      conjectures (checked $m \le 5$; up to four boxes)                                                                      [-@cnj-criterion], [-@cnj-Pim], [-@cnj-structure]
:::

The brane--brane sector of the cover agrees coefficient by coefficient with the $\mathrm{U}(N_A)$ refined LMOV invariants of [@KN17] (§[-@sec-split]) and therefore has, like them, a $G$-expansion with aligned signs. The brane--image sector, after removal of the boundary factors, is aligned except for the $-S\otimes S$ in the switching block, understood as the subtraction of pairs of states. What breaks is the multi-box crosscap part $g$, the sector of fixed points of $\tilde I$, which carries the same universal factor $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)$. The evidence covers the trefoil and $T(2,5)$ with two boxes ($T(2,7)$ for brane--image); the three-box invariants have not been split into brane and image. Thus the positivity problem for refined Kauffman invariants reduces, conjecturally, to adding to the framework of [@KN17] the parity structure of the orientifold: the sign of $\tilde I$ and the multiplet basis of the frozen states.

Several problems remain open. The first is the multiplet structure of the frozen states. The multi-box $c = 1$ part is not $\sigma$-symmetric and cannot be expanded in $G$. By Result [-@exr-multibox-sigma], the component of the asymmetry present in the unrefined theory is removed by the parity rule for $c$, and the remaining refined $\sigma$-odd part is divisible by $(\boldsymbol{t}^2-1)(q_\ell- q_\ell^{-1})$; the $\sigma$-even/odd split is half-integral and the signs do not align for $T(2,5)$, so this split does not suffice for positivity. Going up to $T(2,9)$ with three boxes, and to four boxes for the trefoil, preserves integrality, the position of the $(1+t)$ poles and the universal factor, while the fraction of aligned blocks decreases (Result [-@exr-signs]). The $G$-expansion originates in the structure of oriented surfaces (the Lefschetz $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ on the Hodge decomposition of $H^1$), and there is no reason to expect it for frozen states wrapped on non-orientable surfaces (§[-@sec-sigmaorigin]). Determining the refined handle and crosscap factors of non-orientable surfaces from geometry is the first task.

The second is the separation of $E$ and $C$, which is not determined by the index alone (Proposition [-@prp-EC]). For the lowest fixed sector of two-strand torus knots it is fixed, conjecturally, by the identification of the space of states (§[-@sec-principle]); for the Hopf link $(4,4)$ it is undetermined, and for the sector with two brane and two image boxes of the trefoil it is fixed only up to $\lambda^{-12}$ (Appendix [C.3](#sec-app-n2)). The action on boundary zero modes is fixed (Proposition [-@prp-boundary]); what remains is the moduli part, i.e., the splitting of the $t$-charge into $J_2$ and $S_R$, which the index does not provide. That the cohomological Hall module of [@Young16] is not free over the CoHA is the algebraic form of this ambiguity (for the loop quiver it is determined, consistent with the uniqueness of $E$ for the framed unknot).

The meaning of the universal factor is only partly understood. The factor $(\boldsymbol{a}^2 - \boldsymbol{q}^2)$ is the $\mathrm{SO}(2)$ point and $(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)$ is explained by $t = q$ and parity. Why $\hat g$ is independent of $t$ at the $\mathrm{SO}(2)$ point (Result [-@exr-universal]), whether this follows from a formal continuation to $N = 1$, and the relation of the shift $\lambda \to \tilde\lambda$ to the tripling of the closed-string Kähler variable in [@AM22] (§[-@sec-hopf], Appendix [B](#sec-app-closed)), remain unexplained *(open)*.

Beyond two-strand torus knots the picture is incomplete. For iterated torus knots the DAHA of [@CD14] provides a definition, adopted here for two algebraic cables (§[-@sec-cable]); the sign property fails there, and what survives is integrality and the universal factor. Why the $c = 1$ part is $\sigma$-symmetric only for two-strand torus knots is not understood *(open)*. The Kauffman superpolynomials of [@GW05] are positive for two-strand torus knots; their relation to our $c = 1$ part has not been examined *(open)*. Non-algebraic cables were not treated, and the two- and three-box invariants of $\mathcal{C}_{15}$ are out of reach of the present computation.

For the other classical groups, the two-box $T(2,5)$ of $\mathrm{Sp}(2N)$ needs the values for all $N \le 13$, too costly for the present implementation; whether the relations of §[-@sec-sp] follow from a duality of the $C_N$ and $D_N$ DAHA is open. The closed string of type $B$ [@AM22] has only $c = 1$ and the denominator $(t^{n/2} + t^{-n/2})$; how type $B$ fits the classification of Proposition [-@prp-alld] has not been examined.

Finally, a cell model of the brane--image composite sector together with a real structure on it would fix $E$ from geometry. An exploratory computation with the cell decomposition of [@ORS12] for the trefoil reproduces its HOMFLY homology but shows that the fixed-sector index $\Phi= (1-t)\mathcal{B}$ is not the $\psi^2$ of the fundamental representation of the cover; it factorizes with the same boundary factor $(\lambda^2-1)(q-1)$ as the framed unknot.

Once the multiplet structure of the frozen states is determined, the multi-box sign problem of §[-@sec-positivity] can be formulated as a multi-box version of the sign property of §[-@sec-criterion].

# Appendix A: Computational methods {#sec-app-code .appendix .unnumbered}

All computations were done with the author's Python code (Koornwinder polynomials and the polynomial representations of the DAHA of types $D_N$, $C_N$ and $\mathrm{GL}_N$; rational function arithmetic with FLINT). Its output was checked by the reproduction of the values of [@Marino09], agreement with Kauffman polynomials at $t = q$, agreement with direct fixed-$N$ computations, agreement with the invariants of [@KN17], and the symmetry $R \leftrightarrow R^T$. Two identifications used as input were verified numerically as checks of the implementation: the dual Cauchy identity ([-@eq-mimachi]) for $(n, m) = (1,1), (2,1), (1,2), (2,2), (2,3), (3,2)$, and the identification of the $D_N$ Macdonald dimension $\dim_R$ of [@AgSc12] with the principal specialization of the Koornwinder polynomial for the representations $(1), (2), (1,1), (3), (2,1), (1,1,1)$ at $N = 2, 3$ (against the evaluation formulas of [@vD96; @Sahi99] and against polynomials constructed by the $q$-difference operator).

## A.1 DAHA conventions and checks {#sec-app-daha-conv .unnumbered}

In ([-@eq-JD]) the conventions are: $(T_i - t^{1/2})(T_i + t^{-1/2}) = 0$; since the vector representation is minuscule, $Y_{\varepsilon_1} = \pi_1 T_{u_1}$ with $\pi_1(X_b) = q^{(\omega_{1*}, b)}X_{u_1^{-1}b}$ ($\omega_{1*} = \varepsilon_1$ for $D_N$, $\omega_{1*} \equiv -\varepsilon_N$ for $\mathrm{GL}_N$); $\tau_-(X) = q^{1/2}YX$, $\tau_+(Y) = q^{-1/2}XY$, and $T(2,2m+1)$ corresponds to $\gamma = \tau_+^m\tau_-^2$. To speed up the computation we use the anti-involution $\varphi$ exchanging $X$ and $Y$, symmetrize over orbits, and share intermediate results between representations. The composites $(\alpha;\bar1)$ of the cover are computed by starting the chain of operators on the $X$ side from $\hat\gamma'(p_1(Y))\cdot 1$, where $\hat\gamma' = \varphi\hat\gamma\varphi$ and $p_1(Y)\cdot 1$ is built by symmetrization on the $X^{-1}$ side. For four boxes one needs $|\alpha| = 3$, where the irreducible decomposition $P_\alpha(X)p_1(X^{-1}) = P_{(\alpha;\bar1)}(X) + \sum_\mu c_{\alpha,\mu}P_\mu(X)$ ($\mu = \alpha - \varepsilon_i$) has several lower terms. From $p_1(X^{-1}) = e_{N-1}(X)/e_N(X)$ and the Pieri rule for vertical strips, $c_{\alpha,\mu} = \psi'_{\nu/\alpha}$ with $\nu = \alpha + 1^N - \varepsilon_i$ (the Pieri coefficient $\psi'$ of Chapter VI of [@Macdonald95]); only the leg in column $0$ depends on $N$, which gives a closed form in $t^N$, checked against the polynomial decomposition for small $N$ and against the identity of principal specializations for all $N$. For iterated torus knots (§[-@sec-cable]) the polynomial from the pattern step is expanded in the basis values $\{\hat\gamma_{\mathrm{comp}}(H_\nu)\}$ of the companion step, which are computed with coefficients kept as Laurent polynomials without cancellation.

::: {#exr-daha}
## checks

The implementation was checked as follows. For $D_N$, $\mathrm{GL}_N$ ($N = 2, 3, 4$) the DAHA relations (quadratic, braid, cross, commutativity of $Y$) hold, and the $D_N$ Macdonald polynomials are eigenfunctions of the Macdonald operator. For $C_2$, $C_3$ the DAHA relations hold as well.

On the $D_N$ side, $Z = T_R^{-F}\,\mathop{\mathrm{mirror}}(W_R)$ with $W_R$ the fixed-$N$ invariant in the uniform normalization, for $N = 2, 3$, $R \in \{(1), (1,1), (2)\}$, $m = 1, 2$. For $N = 4, 5$ the fundamental representation coincides exactly with the mirror of (6.15) of [@AgSc12]. On the $\mathrm{GL}_N$ side, ([-@eq-Mb]) holds with $\mathsf{c}_K= m+1$. For $m = 1$ the rule was read off from $(1), (2), (1,1)$ and predicted correctly for $(3), (2,1), (1,1,1)$ and the adjoint ($\mathrm{U}(3)$, $\mathrm{U}(5)$); for $m = 2$ it holds for $(1), (2), (1,1)$ at $N = 2, 3, 4$ (nine cases) and for the adjoint. For composites with $|\alpha| = 3$ the values of $(3;\bar1)$ in $\mathrm{U}(2)$ and $(2,1;\bar1)$, $(1,1,1;\bar1)$ in $\mathrm{U}(4)$ agree exactly with those of $(4)$, $(3,2,1)$, $(2,2,2)$ ($m = 1$).

Two implementations of the DAHA action, a direct one and an optimized one, agree coefficient by coefficient on all computed values.
:::

The largest computations, the three-box $T(2,9)$ on the $D_{14}$ DAHA and one basis value of the $(2,13)$-cable on $D_{15}$, each take between one and a half and two hours and 16 to 19 GB of memory.

## A.2 Interpolation in $N$ {#sec-app-interp .unnumbered}

The interpolation rests on two assumptions, which we have not proved. We assume that the reduced invariant $\mathcal{R}_R(N) = T_R^{-F}\,\mathop{\mathrm{mirror}}(Z(N))/K_R(t^\rho)$ (with $Z$ the unnormalized value of §[-@sec-daha]) is a Laurent polynomial in $U = t^N$ whose coefficients are Laurent polynomials in $q^{1/2}, t^{1/2}$. We also assume a range for the powers of $U$: the minimal and maximal degrees in $t^{1/2}$ of the computed values, as functions of $N$, are observed to become linear, $2Nj_{\min} + \mathrm{const}$ and $2Nj_{\max} + \mathrm{const}$, once $N$ is large enough; the slopes $j_{\min}, j_{\max}$ are read off from consecutive $N$, and the powers $U^j$ are taken to be confined to $j_{\min} \le j \le j_{\max}$. Both assumptions are supported only by the comparison, described below, with the direct computation at values of $N$ not used in the interpolation. With $n = j_{\max} - j_{\min} + 1$ unknown coefficients, Newton's divided differences on $n$ nodes $N$ determine them, and the result is compared coefficient by coefficient with the direct computation at the remaining $N$. When $n$ is large (two boxes of $T(2,7)$ and $T(2,9)$ and their adjoints, three boxes of $T(2,5)$ and beyond, four boxes, composites with $m \ge 2$, two boxes of the cables), the unknowns are restricted degree by degree in $q^{1/2}$: for each degree $\alpha$ of $q^{1/2}$ and each power $U^j$, the coefficient is assumed to have its degrees in $t^{1/2}$ within the range of degrees of the $q^{\alpha/2}$-part of the computed value at a reference $N_0$ (a "band"); the resulting linear system over all nodes is solved and accepted only if it has a unique solution, and the solution is then compared with the values at all $N$ not used. For the $(1,1)$ invariant of $\mathcal{C}_{13}$ the band was chosen separately for each degree $\alpha$, with the smallest $N_0$ for which the system is consistent. The verified ranges are in Tables [-@tbl-interp] and [-@tbl-cableinterp]. In two rows the comparison rests on a single value of $N$: the $(1,1,1)$ invariant of the trefoil is compared at $N = 3$ only, and the $(2)$ invariant of $\mathcal{C}_{15}$, which is not used in the text, at $N = 10$ only.

::: {#exr-interp}
In the ranges of Tables [-@tbl-interp] and [-@tbl-cableinterp] the values at the $N$ not used in the interpolation were predicted coefficient by coefficient. ## A.3 One-probe computation for the Hopf link {#sec-app-virtual .unnumbered}

For the Hopf link with one probe on each component we use the probe basis $K_{(n)}(y; t, q; 1, -1, q^{1/2}, -q^{1/2})$ (monic Askey--Wilson polynomials).

::: {#cnj-c2j}
The coefficient of $y^{n-2j}$ in $K_{(n)}(y; t, q; 1, -1, q^{1/2}, -q^{1/2})$ is, as a rational function of $t^n$, $$
c_{2j}(n) = t^j\, \frac{(q/t; t^2)_j}{(t^2; t^2)_j}\cdot\frac{(1 - t^n)(1 + t^{n-2j})\prod_{i=1}^{j-1}(1 - t^{2n-2i})}{\prod_{i=1}^{j}(1 - qt^{2n-2i-1})} .
$$ {#eq-c2j}
:::

Equation ([-@eq-c2j]) agrees with the recursion for the Askey--Wilson coefficients at four rational points for $j \le 5$, $n \le 30$. With it, the virtual normalization $Z^{\mathrm{virt}} = y_1^N y_2^N Z$ is a polynomial in $y_1, y_2$ whose coefficient of $y_1^a y_2^b$ is a finite sum independent of $N$, so $U$ can be kept as a formal variable in this one-probe computation (full agreement with the direct computation at $U = t^N$, $N = 3, \dots, 8$, for $a + b \le 8$). The multi-probe computations of §[-@sec-kernel] do not use ([-@eq-c2j]).

## A.4 Integer programs for $E$ {#sec-app-ilp .unnumbered}

When $E$ is said to be determined by (E1) and (E2), the following problem was solved. Let $\Phi= \sum_\omega c_\omega\,\omega$ be the index of the fixed sector (a Laurent polynomial in $q^{1/2}, t^{1/2}, \lambda$) and write $E = \sum_\omega e_\omega\,\omega$ with unknown integers $e_\omega$ over the monomials of $\Phi$ (or of a stated larger support). The constraints are: (i) $e_\omega \equiv c_\omega \pmod 2$ (integrality of $f$, §[-@sec-EC]); (ii) $|e_\omega| \le |c_\omega|$ (Hypothesis [-@exm-QP], used for the Hopf link; for knots this bound is replaced by the explicit ansätze of Appendix [C.2](#sec-app-attempts)); (iii) the linear equations (E1), $\sum_\omega e_\omega\,\omega|_{t=-1} = [2(1+t)g]_{t=-1}$ coefficient by coefficient; (iv) when (E2) is imposed, the linear equations $\sum_\omega e_\omega\,\omega|_{t=q} = -(1+q)\psi^2 g^{\mathrm{odd}}$ coefficient by coefficient. Feasibility and uniqueness are decided by solving the integer linear program with an exact solver; "unique" means that the solution set has one element, and "$k$ of $n$ monomials free" means that the affine solution set has dimension $k$ within the $n$ unknowns. The minimal number of exchanged pairs quoted in Appendix [C.3](#sec-app-n2) is the minimum of $\tfrac12\sum_\omega(|c_\omega| - |e_\omega|)$ over the solution set.

# Appendix B: Closed strings {#sec-app-closed .appendix .unnumbered}

::: {#exr-closed}
The $d$-th term of $-\log Z$ built from the $D_N$ product formula $Z = \prod_{m<\beta}\prod_{\alpha>0}(q^{-m/2}t^{-(\alpha,\rho)/2} - q^{m/2}t^{(\alpha,\rho)/2})$, $t = q^\beta$, and the three terms of §6 of [@AgSc12], $$
\frac{1}{2d}\frac{\mathsf{Q}^d t^{d/2} q^{-d/2}}{z_q(q^d) z_t(t^d)} + \frac1d \frac{(\mathsf{Q} t/q)^{d/2}}{z_q(q^d)} - \frac{1}{2d}\frac{\mathsf{Q}^d t^{d/2}q^{-d/2}}{z_q(q^d)(t^{d/2} + t^{-d/2})},\qquad \mathsf{Q} = t^{2N-1},
$$ {#eq-AgSc3} differ only by terms linear in $N$ (classical terms and constant maps), for $N = 2, \dots, 7$.
:::

The three terms of ([-@eq-AgSc3]) are the closed-string version of Proposition [-@prp-alld]: $\mathbb{P}^1$ is an invariant state with $\varepsilon = +1$, and the sum of the first and third terms is the contribution of the even $z_2$ modes only; $\mathbb{RP}^2$ is a frozen state, the second term.

In [@AM22] the same partition function is written with multiple sine functions, and the $D$- and $C$-type free energies are organized into three pieces: a $c = 1$ term for odd $n$, a "Klein bottle" ($c = 2$) term for all $n$, and a "tripling" of the Kähler variable. From here on $(Q, T)$ and $\mathsf X$ denote the variables of [@AM22]; the Kähler variable of ([-@eq-AgSc3]) is written $\mathsf{Q}$.

::: {#prp-AM}
In the variables $(Q, T) = (q^{1/2}, t^{1/2})$ of [@AM22], let $\mathsf X = e^{\tau_1/2}$, $e^{\tau_2} = \mathsf X^2/Q$, $e^{\tau_0} = \mathsf X^2 T/Q$. Then, as rational functions for each $n$, $$
\underbrace{-\frac{\mathsf X^{2n}}{2n(Q^{2n} - Q^{-2n})}}_{\text{odd-$n$ correction}}
+ \underbrace{\frac{e^{n\tau_2}}{2n}\frac{Q^n T^{-n} - T^n Q^{-n}}{(Q^{2n} - Q^{-2n})(T^n + T^{-n})}}_{\text{Klein bottle}}
= -\frac{e^{n\tau_0}}{2n\,(Q^n - Q^{-n})(T^n + T^{-n})} .
$$ {#eq-AM} Hence "odd-$n$ $c = 1$ plus Klein bottle" of [@AM22] equals the sum of the frozen-state term $e^{n\tau_1/2}/(n(Q^n - Q^{-n}))$ for all $n$ and the term of invariant states with $\varepsilon = +1$. The Klein bottle term and its numerator $Q^n/T^n - T^n/Q^n$ are not an independent multiplet: they are the difference between $-\tfrac12\psi^2 C$ and $\tfrac12 E/(1+t)$ when the expansion is organized by odd $d$ ($E \ne \psi^2 C$).
:::

::: {.proof}
Bringing the left-hand side to a common denominator, the coefficient of $\mathsf X^{2n}$ is $[-(T^n + T^{-n}) + Q^{-n}(Q^nT^{-n} - T^nQ^{-n})]/(\cdots) = -T^nQ^{-n}(Q^n + Q^{-n})/(\cdots)$, and $(Q^{2n} - Q^{-2n}) = (Q^n - Q^{-n})(Q^n + Q^{-n})$ cancels.
:::

The conventions of [@AM22] and [@AgSc12] are related by $(q, t, Q) \to (q^{-1}, t^{-1}, Q^{-1})$ and an overall sign ($\log Z$ versus $-\log Z$). The ratio of charges of frozen and oriented states is $x^2/Q_0 = q_r^{-1}$ in [@AgSc12] and $w = q_r$ in [@AM22].

We end with a comment on handle factors. In our reading, the "difference $\times$ sum" $(q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})$ in the derivation of strong integrality in §4 of [@AgSc12] is $\psi^2 z$, obtained when the $c = 1$ contribution of the class $\beta/2$ is placed at doubled $d$, rather than the factor of a single handle; in the M-theory interpretation of [@PU14], the twisted trace of a single $\tilde I$-invariant handle of the cover is one factor of $z$ in the same variables. After refinement $G = z_q z_t = T_+T_-$ with $T_\pm = (q_\ell^{1/2} - q_\ell^{-1/2}) \pm (q_r^{1/2} - q_r^{-1/2})$. However, $T_\pm$ do not make a $\sigma$-asymmetric $c = 1$ part expandable: the elements of $\mathbb{Z}[q_r^{\pm 1}][T_+, T_-] = \mathbb{Z}[q_r^{\pm1}][q_\ell^{1/2} - q_\ell^{-1/2}, q_r^{1/2} - q_r^{-1/2}]$ with integer powers of $q_\ell$ are sums of even powers of $(q_\ell^{1/2} - q_\ell^{-1/2})$ and hence invariant under $q_\ell\to q_\ell^{-1}$.

# Appendix C: Further structure of the fixed sector {#sec-app-fixed .appendix .unnumbered}

This appendix collects the results on the fixed sector of the cover that go beyond the identification of §[-@sec-principle]: the generating functions of the corrections, other torus knots, composites, the attempts to determine $E$ for knots from the index, and the sector with two brane and two image boxes. The notation is that of §[-@sec-cover]; $V' := 1 + q + qt$.

## C.1 Generating functions and other torus knots {.unnumbered}

::: {#exr-plog}
The plethystic logarithm of the generating function of $X_{j'}$ is finite ($(1+2t+qt)z - t^2z^2$: the Fock space of $V\oplus t$ with the relation $t^2z^2$), but those of $F_{j'}$ in ([-@eq-Fgen]) and of the upper series $\mathrm{Sym}^jV + (q-t)t^{m-1-j'}F_{j'}$ are infinite; the generators of the latter are $Vz$ and $(q-t)t^{m-1-j'}c_{j'}z^{m+j'}$ ($c_0 = 1$, $c_1 = V^2 - t(1+qt)$, negative coefficients from $c_2$ on). The upper series cannot be read as a Fock space of positive BPS generators.
:::

::: {#exr-t34}
For the three-strand knot $T(3,4)$ ($\gamma = \tau_+\tau_-^3$, $K = 9$) the following parts of Conjecture [-@cnj-closedform] hold: the lower series $\mathrm{Sym}^kV$, the subtraction of a perfect square at the switching block $k = 2\delta$, $K = rs - 3$, and the existence of an $E$ satisfying (E1) and (E2). But the factor of the square is $\tilde S = (1+qt)(1+t+t^2+qt^2+q^2t^2)$ (10 states), not the reduced superpolynomial of $T(3,4)$ (11 states), and the upper series is not of the form $-t^{K-2j}[\mathrm{Sym}^jV + (q-t)R_j]$ ($-t^8(q+t)$ at $j = 0$). The integer program with the lower series fixed has solutions under (E1) and (E2) but not a unique one (29 of 111 monomials undetermined).
:::

::: {#exr-threestrand}
In this Result a torus knot with $p$ strands is written $T(r,s)$ with $s = p < r$ (so the knot called $T(3,4)$ in the text has $r = 4$, $s = 3$). For three strands the upper series $\mathcal U_j := -n_{K-j}/t^{K-2j}$ has the form $(1 + q/t)\mathrm{Sym}^jV + (q-t)C_j$ for $j \le \delta - 2$ ($C_j$ depends on the knot), and at $j = \delta - 1$ a perfect square at $t = q$, $-([\lfloor r/2\rfloor]_{t^2}[r']_t)^2/t^{\delta-1}$ with $[n]_x = (1 - x^n)/(1-x)$ and $r'$ the largest odd number $\le r$, enters ($T(3,4)$, $T(3,5)$, $T(3,7)$, $T(3,8)$, $T(3,10)$). For four strands ($T(4,5)$, $T(4,7)$) the prefactor is $h_2(q,t)/t^2$, the square sits at $j = r - s + 1$, and its factor reads $\rho_0(T(s-1, r-s+1))\cdot S(T(2,r'))|_{t=q}$. For $E$, the switching rule $E_{2\delta} = \mathrm{Sym}^{2\delta}V|_{\varepsilon} - \psi^2\tilde S$ (where $|_\varepsilon$ denotes the insertion of the signs of $\tilde I$) is compatible with (E1) and (E2) also for $T(3,4)$, $T(3,5)$, and the two deepest blocks are unique ($E_K = -t^8(q-t)$, $+t^{11}(q-t)$). For two strands, splitting $E$ in the same $(R, \Gamma)$ form as Proposition [-@prp-rows], the $\tilde I$ on the rows of $\Gamma$ is the rule $q \mapsto -q$ in the deep rows ($j \ge \delta + 2$) and a pair correction $D_{\delta-i} = t^{a(m,i)}\tilde D_i$ above, where $\tilde D_i$ is a polynomial depending only on the parities of $i$ and $m$ and $a(m,i)$ an integer exponent.
:::

::: {#exr-composite}
## factorization of composites at large $N$

The relation $A = R^2 + (q-1)(t-1)\Gamma$ of Proposition [-@prp-rows] is not limited to the adjoint. The large-$N$ values of the composites $(2;\bar1)$, $(1,1;\bar1)$, $(2;\bar2)$, $(2;\overline{1,1})$, $(1,1;\overline{1,1})$ of the trefoil satisfy $R_{(\alpha;\bar\beta)} = R_\alpha R_\beta + (q-1)(t-1)\Gamma_{\alpha\beta}$ (the top row is the product, the difference is divisible by $(q-1)(t-1)$ in every row), and the rows of $\Gamma_{\alpha\beta}$ contain dimension-type factors $(1+q)$, $(1+t)$ according to $\alpha, \beta$. The factor $(q-1)(t-1)$ is the refined measure of the annular string between brane and image, and the integrality of $\mathcal{N}$ is equivalent to LMOV-type integrality of the connected correlator (an interpretation). The generalization $\rho_0^\alpha\rho_1^\beta + \rho_1^\alpha\rho_0^\beta - \rho_1^\alpha\rho_1^\beta$ of $\gamma_1 = (2\rho_0\rho_1 - \rho_1^2)/q$ does not hold for other composites.
:::

::: {#rem-pairblind}
*Remark 61*. The sign of $\tilde I$ on a pair $(q\mu, -t\mu)$ of the $(q-t)$ correction does not appear in condition (E2), since the pair vanishes at $t = q$; hence (E2) imposes no constraint on these signs. Since (E1) alone does not fix them either (computation: 2 of 15 signs for $j' = 2$ at $n = 1$, 3 of 17 for $R = (2)$ at $n = 2$), a structure of the space of states such as Conjecture [-@cnj-closedform] is needed.
:::

## C.2 Attempts to determine $E$ for knots from the index {#sec-app-attempts .unnumbered}

::: {#exr-EC}
## negative

The following attempts to determine $E$ for knots were made, with the integer programs of Appendix [A.4](#sec-app-ilp).

We first tried partial sums of states. As for the Hopf link, write $E = \Phi- 2\Phi_-$ with $\Phi= (1-t)\mathcal{B}$, and impose (a) $C$ integer Laurent and (b) the form of (E2), $E|_{t=q} = -(1+q)\psi^2(g_{\ydA} + 1)$. There is no solution for the trefoil (the computation was not run for $T(2,5)$). Even without the range constraint, no $E$ satisfying (a) and (b) fits inside the monomial support of $\Phi$.

Next we tried an ansatz of Adams type, $E = F\cdot(\psi^2[g_{\ydA}] + 1)$ with $F$ among $(1+q)$, $(1+t)$, $(q+t)$, $(1+qt)$ and their monomial multiples, allowing $\psi^2$ to multiply $\lambda^2$ by $(q/t)^{j/2}$, $|j| \le 2$; none satisfies (a).

Twisted traces were tried as well. We write the fixed-sector index as $\Phi= t^{1/2} z_q \Phi_k$, take a twisted character of $\tilde I$ for each multiplet of $\Phi_k$ (terms of the $G$-expansion or monomials), and solve $E = t^{1/2}Z_\partial\sum_\omega e_\omega\tilde b_\omega$, $|e_\omega| \le |c_\omega|$, $e_\omega \equiv c_\omega \pmod 2$, with boundary factor $Z_\partial$, as an integer program. The twisting rule is hypothetical; we tried $\pi$ rotations in the $q$ and $t$ planes and monomial-wise signs. The Hopf $E_{22}, E_{24}$ are reproduced uniquely with $Z_\partial = z_q$ and monomial-wise signs. For knots the target values at $t = q$ and $t = -1$ both contain $(1+q)$, so there is no solution with $Z_\partial = z_q$; the boundary factor must be the sum $z_q^+$, as derived in Proposition [-@prp-boundary]. With $Z_\partial = z_q^+$ the trefoil is solvable uniquely but the solution shows no regularity, and $T(2,5)$ has no solution for any rule; relaxing the bound $|c_\omega|$ requires at least two invariant pairs not visible in $\Phi$.

In a further integer program, with the boundary factor fixed to $z_q^+$ and a handle twist $G\to \chi$ ($\chi\in\{z_q, z_t, (z_q+z_t)/2, (qt)^{1/2}-(qt)^{-1/2}, z_q^+-z_t^+\}$) on the multiplets of the $G$-expansion of the moduli part, there is no solution for $T(2,3)$, $T(2,5)$.

Sign rules fail too. For the Hopf $(2,2)$ a sign rule by the parities of the exponents of $t$ and $\lambda$ reproduces $E_{22}$, but for the Hopf $(2,4)$ and for knots neither this type of rule (8 rules with 4 offsets) nor the 36 rules combining signs with handle twists satisfy (E1) and (E2). For knots, states of equal charge carry different signs.
:::

## C.3 The sector brane 2, image 2 {#sec-app-n2 .unnumbered}

We summarize the results for the fixed sector $n = 2$ (two brane and two image boxes) of the trefoil. $E$ is determined up to $\lambda^{-12}$ and undetermined from $\lambda^{-14}$ on. Notation: the rows of the mirror images of the fundamental and two-box representations are written $R_{\ydA} = a_2\lambda^{-2} + a_4\lambda^{-4}$, $R_{\ydB} = b_4\lambda^{-4} + b_6\lambda^{-6} + b_8\lambda^{-8}$, $R_{\ydAA} = c_4\lambda^{-4} + \cdots$, those of the adjoint $g^{\mathrm{adj}}_j$, and those of the composites $\Gamma_{\alpha\beta}$ (Result [-@exr-composite]); the "background" is the part of the fixed sector that survives when all Wilson loop data are set to their unknot values, and its "cells" are the monomials generating it as a Fock space.

::: {#exr-n2rows}
## rows of $n = 2$ and the $R$ dependence

The fixed sector $\mathcal{N}_R$ of $n = 2$ for the trefoil ($R = (2), (1,1)$) can be written explicitly as a polynomial (of degree at most four) in the rows $a_j$ ($a_2 = (1+qt)/q$, $a_4 = -t/q$), $b_j$, $c_j$, $g^{\mathrm{adj}}_j$ and $\Gamma_{\alpha\beta}$; with the actual rows it agrees with the computed $\mathcal{N}_R$ in all blocks up to $\lambda^{-20}$. It has three properties.

It is covariant under a reweighting of the rows, denoted $\sigma$ in this Result (it is not the involution $\sigma$ of §[-@sec-variables]). Under the reweighting $\sigma$ of the two-box rows and of $\Gamma$, $b_j \mapsto qb_j$, $c_j \mapsto c_j/t$, $\Gamma_{\alpha\beta} \mapsto w_\alpha w_\beta \Gamma_{\alpha\beta}$ ($w_{\ydB} = q$, $w_{\ydAA} = 1/t$), the difference $\mathcal{N}_{\ydB}\circ\sigma - \mathcal{N}_{\ydAA}$ is $(q-t)\times$ a polynomial in the adjoint-sector symbols $a_2, a_4, g^{\mathrm{adj}}_j$ and the background alone (up to $\lambda^{-20}$). The $R$ dependence thus splits into a reweighting of the two-box rows and a tower "two vacuum states $(q-t)\otimes$ adjoint".

At $\lambda^{-12}$ the $\sigma$-covariant part is a perfect square $-(t^{3/2}/q^{1/2})\hat Y_R^2$ for both $R$, with $\hat Y_{\ydAA} = (1+q)(1+t)(1+qt)/q^3$ and $\hat Y_{\ydB} = [(1+q)(1+t)(1+qt)^2 + qt(q-t)]/q^4$ (10 monomials, positive, irreducible, not a product). The correction is $(q-t)[(t/q^4)a_2^2 + \eta]$ with $\eta = [tV'^2a_2^2/q^3 - 2a_2\tilde\Sigma + (V'-t)g^{\mathrm{adj}}_6]/q^3$ ($\tilde\Sigma = (1+t+qt)/q$; $\eta = 0$ for $R = (1,1)$). Distinguishing the brane and image rows by different symbols, this square is literally the tensor product of a brane object and its image.

Finally, $\hat Y_R$ is a single-brane quantity. The two-box cumulants of a single brane ($\log$ of $W_{\ydA}, W_{\ydB}, W_{\ydAA}$ with the Adams term $f_{\ydB} = Z_{\ydB} - \tfrac12\psi^2 Z_{\ydA}$) projected onto the Schur $R$, $\Omega^{(0)}_R(\lambda) = \sum_\rho \chi_R(\rho)f_\rho/z_\rho$, equal a prefactor $-q^{1/2}t/(t-1)$ times $[\Omega'_2\lambda^{-2} + \Omega'_4\lambda^{-4} + \cdots]$, and exactly $\Omega'_4 = \hat Y_R$ for both $R$. The $qt(q-t)$ in $\hat Y_{\ydB}$ comes from the Adams term. For $R = (1,1)$ the correction is also the square of $\Omega'_2 = -a_2/q$: $\mathcal{N}_{12}(1,1) = -(t^{3/2}/q^{1/2})[\Omega_4'^2 + (q-t)(t/q^2)\Omega_2'^2]$.
:::

::: {#exr-tower}
## generating function of the adjoint tower

Let $\xi = \lambda^{-2}$. The kernels in $\mathcal{N}_{\ydB}\circ\sigma - \mathcal{N}_{\ydAA} = -(t^{3/2}/q^{1/2})(q-t)[R_{\ydA}(\xi)^2\kappa_R(\xi) + \Gamma_{\mathrm{adj}}(\xi)\kappa_\Gamma(\xi) + \beta(\xi)]$ are, in closed form, $$
\kappa_\Gamma(\xi) = \frac{q^2\xi^3[\,q^2(V'-t) - t^2\xi(V-q)\,]}{(t\xi-q)(t^3\xi-q)(t^2\xi-q^2)(t\xi-q^3)},\qquad
\beta(\xi) = \frac{-q^2\xi^4}{(\xi-q)(t\xi-q)(t^2\xi-q)(t\xi-q^2)(t\xi-1)},
$$ {#eq-kernels1}

$$\kappa_R(\xi) = \frac{-q^2\xi^3\,P_5(\xi)}{(\xi-q)(t\xi-q)(t^2\xi-q)(t^3\xi-q)(t\xi-q^2)(t^2\xi-q^2)(t\xi-q^3)(t\xi-1)},
$$ {#eq-kernels2} with $P_5$ an irreducible polynomial of degree five in $\xi$. They were obtained by running the computation with the two-box rows and $\Gamma$ set to zero as rational functions in $\lambda$ (agreeing with the series in symbolic blocks up to $\lambda^{-20}$). All kernels are "two vacuum states $(q-t)\times$ Fock kernels of cells", the cells being the six background cells ($t, 1/q, t/q, t^2/q, t/q^2$; $t^2/q^2$) plus $t^3/q, t/q^3$ specific to $\Gamma_{\mathrm{adj}}$. The series coefficients of $\kappa_\Gamma$ are of staircase type, $t^nT_nU_n/q^{3(n+1)}$ with $T_n = \sum_{0\le j\le i\le n}q^it^j$ and $U_n$ a polynomial of degree $n$ in $q, t$ (not reproduced here).
:::

::: {#exr-n2E}
## $E$ at $\lambda^{-12}$ for $n = 2$: full exchange

At $\lambda^{-12}$ the $E$ of $n = 2$ is, for both $R$, "signs of the background cells plus the exchange $\psi^2$ on all squares and products of rows of the knot part", and satisfies (E1) and (E2): $$\begin{gathered}
E_{12}(1,1) = q^{-13/2}t^{3/2}\bigl[\psi^2\hat Y_{\ydAA} + (q-t)(t/q^2)\,\psi^2\Omega'_2\bigr] - B_{12}(1,1),\\
B_{12}(1,1) = -q^{-13/2}t^{3/2}(q-t)qt^2 .
\end{gathered}$$ {#eq-E12} The term $-B_{12}$ is the $E$ of the background ($E_B = -B$). For $R = (2)$, besides the square $\psi^2\hat Y_{\ydB}$, each piece of the correction is fixed including its sign. The pieces $(t/q^4)a_2^2$ and $tV'^2a_2^2/q^6$ are replaced by their $\psi^2$, and the cross term $-2a_2\tilde\Sigma$ by $0$. The top row of $\Gamma_{\mathrm{adj}}$ is treated by the same exchange as for $n = 1$, $\gamma_1 = (2\rho_0\rho_1 - \rho_1^2)/q \mapsto -\rho_1^2/q$, and its kernel $V' - t$ becomes $(1+q)(1-t)$ by the cell sign $(-1)^{\deg_q\deg_t}$; this is one of 16 sign choices for the kernel. This $E$ does not satisfy the bound $|e_\omega| \le |c_\omega|$ monomial by monomial on the correction. The block signs are unified as $(-1)^{k/2+1}$ ($k$ the exponent in $\lambda^{-k}$) across the $n = 1$ switching block, $\lambda^{-10}$ of $R = (2)$ and $\lambda^{-12}$ of both $R$, corresponding to flipping the sign of one cell in the signed version of $F_{j'}$ for $n = 1$. By the same rule the second term $V - q$ in the numerator of $\kappa_\Gamma$ becomes $(1-q)(1+t)$ (a conjecture).
:::

::: {#exr-n2negative}
## obstruction from $\lambda^{-14}$ on; negative

With the $E$ of $\lambda^{-8}$--$\lambda^{-12}$ fixed, the integer program at $\lambda^{-14}$ determines only 2--3 of 113 unknowns even under (E1) and (E2) (the minimal number of exchanged pairs is 48 under (E1), 936 under (E1) and (E2)). A construction taking the trace of the exchange monomial by monomial in the symbolic blocks does not give an $E$ for any assignment of brane/image labels (either $R$-independent or not Laurent): the Laurent property of $\mathcal{N}$ arises from cancellations between monomials of different content, so the trace is defined only on the brane object $\hat Y_R = \Omega'_4$ in the Schur basis. Pure brane$\times$image products cancel in the mixed cumulant (rank 0), and the square $\hat Y_R^2$ is carried by the connected kernels (the dimension correction of the composite and the contraction term $\kappa$). At $\lambda^{-14}$ the $\sigma$-covariant part is not divisible by $\hat Y_R$ and cannot be written as a product series at the level of $\Omega^{(0)}$.
:::

## D.2 Reduced invariants of the trefoil at general $N$ from the DAHA {#sec-app-daha .unnumbered}

$\mathcal{R}_{\ydA}(t^N)$ (coefficients of $(t^N)^j$): $$\begin{align*}

\end{align*}$$

$\mathcal{R}_{\ydB}(t^N)$ (coefficients of $(t^N)^j$): $$\begin{align*}
[(t^N)^{-10}]\colon\ & q^{-9} t^{10} -q^{-9} t^{9} -q^{-10} t^{9} +q^{-10} t^{8} \\

## D.4 Brane--brane and brane--image sectors of the cover {#sec-app-cover .unnumbered}

Evidence for §[-@sec-split]. For the two-box trefoil and $T(2,5)$, the sectors of the generating function of the cover split into brane ($Y$) and image ($Y'$), expanded in $G$ with the $t$-side $(t^{-1/2} - t^{1/2})\hat f$ of [@KN17] (per $\lambda^\beta$, $q_r= (q/t)^{1/2}$). Brane--brane is $\hat f_{\ydB}$, $\hat f_{\ydAA}$ (hatted with $M \otimes M$); brane--image is $\mathcal{B}= W_{(1;\bar1)} + \kappa - W_{\ydA}^2$ divided by $z_q$; $\mathcal{N}$ is the brane--image sector with all boundary factors removed. The sign classification per block is given in Table [-@tbl-coversplit]: brane--brane is aligned in every block, while $\mathcal{B}/z_q$ mixes "aligned", "$(\boldsymbol{t}^2 - 1)\times$ aligned" and "mixed", and for $\mathcal{N}$ the only mixed block is the switching block $k = 2m$.
